# codelaw — every rule

> 657 rules in 18 packs, plus 23 engine rules. Generated by `scripts/rule-docs.py` from the rule files; one page per rule, with every configuration form, is under https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/.

## Configuring any rule

```toml
preview = true                                   # every pack rule is preview today
extends = ["codelaw:js/recommended"]             # a preset turns rules on and loads its pack

[rules]
"js/no-console" = "warn"                         # a severity: error | warn | info | off
"js/max-params" = { severity = "error", options = { max = 4 } }   # severity and options
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends` (install `@codelaw/rules-<pack>` or `codelaw-rules-<pack>`).
- **Fix kinds:** `auto` — `codelaw fix` applies it; `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; `manual` — follow *How to fix*.
- **Suppress a finding:** a `codelaw-ignore <rule>: <reason>` comment in the language's comment form, e.g. `// codelaw-ignore js/no-console: <reason>`; a reason is required.

## `css-modules/class-naming` — CSS Module class names can be read as styles.name

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css-modules` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming a class must update every file that reads it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css-modules/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css-modules/class-naming.md

### What it checks

A class of a CSS Module is named so that JavaScript reads it as `styles.name`: camelCase by default. With `style = "kebab"` it is kebab-case instead, and `any` turns the check off.

**Why:** `.btn-primary` is `styles["btn-primary"]` and cannot be `styles.btn-primary`; a name that needs brackets is easy to mistype and is not found by a search for `styles.btnPrimary`.

The bundler's `localsConvention` (`[css] modules_convention`) counts: under `camelCase` or `dashes` a kebab-case class is reached as `styles.btnPrimary`, so it passes. Classes inside `:global(…)` are not checked.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `style` | `string` | `"camelCase"` | `camelCase` (a name `styles.x` reaches without brackets), `kebab` (kebab-case) or `any` (no check) |

### How to fix

1. Rename the class (and every `styles.…` that reads it) to camelCase.
2. Or set `[css] modules_convention = "camelCase"` if the bundler already maps the names.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css files
/* src/button.module.css */
.btn-primary { color: red; }
```

##### Do

```css files
/* src/button.module.css */
.btnPrimary { color: red; }
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss files
/* src/button.module.scss */
.btn-primary { color: red; }
```

##### Do

```scss files
/* src/button.module.scss */
.btnPrimary { color: red; }
```

## `css-modules/composes-valid` — composes points at a class that exists

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css-modules` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (which class to compose is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css-modules/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:css-modules/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css-modules/composes-valid.md

### What it checks

`composes` names classes the file or the module it points at defines, and stands in a rule whose selector is one top-level class.

**Why:** a bundler resolves `composes` when it builds, and what it cannot resolve is an error at build time, or a class that quietly does nothing.

It reports `composes: a from "./b.module.css"` when `b.module.css` does not exist or defines no `.a`, a local `composes: a` with no `.a` in the file, and a `composes` inside a nested rule, an at-rule, or a rule whose selector is not one class. `from global` and a package path (`from "lib/x.css"`) are not judged.

### How to fix

1. Correct the class name or the path.
2. Move `composes` into the rule whose selector is the one class that composes.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css files
/* src/button.module.css */
.primary { composes: base from "./base.module.css"; }
/* src/base.module.css */
.root { color: red; }
```

##### Do

```css files
/* src/button.module.css */
.primary { composes: base from "./base.module.css"; }
/* src/base.module.css */
.base { color: red; }
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss files
/* src/button.module.scss */
.primary { composes: base; }
```

##### Do

```scss files
/* src/button.module.scss */
.base { color: red; }
.primary { composes: base; }
```

## `css-modules/no-global` — A CSS Module stays local

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css-modules` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (a global selector exists to reach markup outside the module, which is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css-modules/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css-modules/no-global.md

### What it checks

A CSS Module has no `:global` selector.

**Why:** `:global` leaves the module's scope: the rule can match, and be matched by, any element on the page, which is what modules exist to prevent. Put global rules in a plain stylesheet.

### How to fix

1. Move the rule into a plain `.css` file, or give the markup a local class.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css files
/* src/page.module.css */
:global(.dark) .page { color: white; }
```

##### Do

```css files
/* src/page.module.css */
.dark .page { color: white; }
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss files
/* src/page.module.scss */
:global(.dark) .page { color: white; }
```

##### Do

```scss files
/* src/page.module.scss */
.dark .page { color: white; }
```

## `css-modules/no-undefined-class` — A CSS Module class that is read exists

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css-modules` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to add the class or fix the name is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css-modules/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:css-modules/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css-modules/no-undefined-class.md

### What it checks

`styles.name` reads a class the imported CSS Module defines. The finding is in the JavaScript or TypeScript file, at the name.

**Why:** reading a class the module does not define gives `undefined`, so the element silently loses its style; a typo or a renamed class shows up only on screen.

What the module defines counts `:export` keys and `@value` names, and the names `[css] modules_convention` makes reachable (`.btn-primary` is `styles.btnPrimary` under `camelCase`). A module whose class names the rule cannot work out (Sass interpolation, `&-suffix` on a selector list) is left alone, and so is a computed access such as `styles[name]`.

### How to fix

1. Correct the name in the JavaScript or TypeScript file, or add the class to the module.
2. If the bundler maps names (`localsConvention`), set `[css] modules_convention` so the mapped names count.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.js
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const card = styles.cards;
```

##### Do

```js files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.js
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const card = styles.card;
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.cards} />;
```

##### Do

```jsx files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.ts
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const card: string = styles["cards"];
```

##### Do

```ts files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.ts
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const card: string = styles["card"];
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.tsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.cards} />;
```

##### Do

```tsx files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.tsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

### Differences from the source

eslint-plugin-css-modules's `no-undef-class` needs the stylesheet's path in each import; this rule follows the import through the project graph, and understands `[css] modules`, `composes`, `:export` and `@value`.

## `css-modules/no-unused-class` — A CSS Module class is read somewhere

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css-modules` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a class can be read by a name built at run time or by code outside the repo, so deleting its rule needs a person to accept the diff)
- **Severity when named:** `warn` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css-modules/recommended` at `warn` · `codelaw:css-modules/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css-modules/no-unused-class.md

### What it checks

Every class a CSS Module defines is read by a JavaScript or TypeScript file that imports the module: `styles.name`, `styles["name"]`, `const { name } = styles`, `import { name } from "./x.module.css"`, or composed by another class with `composes`.

**Why:** a class nobody reads is dead CSS that every page downloads, and it hides the classes the component really uses.

A module is left alone when any importer reads it by a computed name (`styles[name]`, `styles[\`btn-${size}\`]`), spreads it, or passes it to a function: the rule cannot tell which classes that reaches, so it reports none rather than guess. A module no file imports is left alone too.

### How to fix

1. Search for the class: `styles.name`, a bracket access, and any `composes` that names it.
2. If a component builds the name at run time, read it by a plain `styles.name` somewhere, or accept that this module is dynamic.
3. Otherwise delete the rule (`codelaw fix --unsafe` does it when the class is the rule's only selector).

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.legacy { color: red; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

##### Do

```css files
/* src/Card.module.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.css";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss files
/* src/Card.module.scss */
$gap: 1rem;
.card { padding: $gap; }
.legacy { color: red; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.scss";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

##### Do

```scss files
/* src/Card.module.scss */
$gap: 1rem;
.card { padding: $gap; }
// src/Card.jsx
import styles from "./Card.module.scss";
export const Card = () => <div className={styles.card} />;
```

### Differences from the source

eslint-plugin-css-modules's `no-unused-class` reads one JS file against its stylesheet; this rule reads the project, so a module imported from several files is judged by all of them, `composes` counts as a use, and a computed access silences the module (the plugin's `camelCase` option is `[css] modules_convention`).

## `css/alpha-value-notation` — Alpha values are percentages

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (old browsers accept only numbers for alpha in `rgba()`)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/alpha-value-notation.md

### What it checks

The alpha channel of a colour function is written as a percentage (`50%`, not `0.5`). The opacity properties (`opacity`, `fill-opacity`, `flood-opacity`, `stop-opacity`, `stroke-opacity`) take numbers instead.

**Why:** One notation for alpha makes values easier to compare at a glance.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `exceptProperties` | `string[]` | `["opacity", "fill-opacity", "flood-opacity", "stop-opacity", "stroke-opacity"]` | properties whose alpha is a number |

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5);
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: rgb(0 0 0 / 50%);
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  color: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: rgb(0 0 0 / 50%);
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `percentage`; the `number` setting is not offered.

## `css/annotation-no-unknown` — No unknown `!` annotations

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended annotation is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/annotation-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

A declaration ends in no `!` annotation other than `!important`.

**Why:** A misspelt annotation such as `!imprtant` makes the browser drop the whole declaration.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreAnnotations` | `string[]` | `[]` | annotations to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### How to fix

1. Correct the spelling to `!important`, or remove the annotation.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: green !imprtant;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: green !important;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  color: green !imprtant;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: green !important;
}
```

## `css/at-rule-descriptor-no-unknown` — No unknown descriptors inside at-rules

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to remove or move the declaration is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/at-rule-descriptor-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Inside `@font-face`, `@counter-style`, `@property`, `@font-palette-values`, `@page`, `@view-transition`, `@color-profile` and `@font-feature-values`, every declaration is a descriptor that at-rule defines.

**Why:** An at-rule ignores descriptors it does not define, so a misplaced property silently does nothing.

### How to fix

1. Check the descriptor name against the at-rule's specification.
2. Fix its spelling, or move the declaration into a style rule where it applies.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("inter.woff2");
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("inter.woff2");
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("inter.woff2");
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("inter.woff2");
}
```

## `css/at-rule-descriptor-value-no-unknown` — No unknown keyword values for at-rule descriptors

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended value is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/at-rule-descriptor-value-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Descriptors that take a fixed set of keywords — `font-display`, `system`, `inherits`, `navigation` and the like — use one of them, and the `syntax` of `@property` is a string.

**Why:** The browser drops a descriptor with a value it does not recognise, so the at-rule falls back to its default.

### How to fix

1. Replace the value with one the descriptor accepts.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("inter.woff2");
  font-display: quick;
}
```

##### Do

```css
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("inter.woff2");
  font-display: swap;
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("inter.woff2");
  font-display: quick;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@font-face {
  font-family: "Inter";
  src: url("inter.woff2");
  font-display: swap;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Checks keyword-valued descriptors and the `@property` `syntax` type only; stylelint validates every descriptor value against the full CSSTree grammar, whose data derives from MDN data (CC0), which codelaw does not ship.

## `css/at-rule-no-deprecated` — No deprecated at-rules

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/at-rule-no-deprecated.md

### What it checks

The sheet uses no at-rule that was removed from or deprecated by the CSS specifications: `@viewport`, `@document` and `@nest`.

**Why:** Browsers dropped or never shipped these at-rules, so what they wrap does not apply.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreAtRules` | `string[]` | `[]` | at-rules to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
.card {
  @nest .theme-dark & {
    color: white;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
.card {
  .theme-dark & {
    color: white;
  }
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.card {
  @nest .theme-dark & {
    color: white;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.card {
  .theme-dark & {
    color: white;
  }
}
```

### Differences from the source

Only `@nest` has a fix (drop the keyword); `@viewport` and `@document` are reported without one.

## `css/at-rule-no-unknown` — No unknown at-rules

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended at-rule is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/at-rule-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Every at-rule is one the CSS specifications define (a vendor prefix is allowed).

**Why:** A browser skips an at-rule it does not know, block and all, so a typo silently disables its contents.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreAtRules` | `string[]` | `[]` | at-rules to accept, such as a preprocessor's; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### How to fix

1. Correct the at-rule name.
2. If a build tool handles it (`@tailwind`, `@include`), add it to `ignoreAtRules`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@keyframe fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

### Differences from the source

On `.scss` files `scss/at-rule-no-unknown` takes this rule's place: it knows Sass's own at-rules.

## `css/at-rule-no-vendor-prefix` — No vendor-prefixed at-rules

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (browsers that need the prefix lose the rule)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/at-rule-no-vendor-prefix.md

### What it checks

At-rules a build tool prefixes, such as `@-webkit-keyframes`, are written without the prefix.

**Why:** Prefixing is a build step; hand-written prefixes go stale and duplicate code.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreAtRules` | `string[]` | `[]` | at-rules to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@-webkit-keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@-webkit-keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

## `css/at-rule-prelude-no-invalid` — At-rule preludes follow their grammar

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended prelude is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/at-rule-prelude-no-invalid.md

### What it checks

The prelude of an at-rule — what comes between its name and its block — has the shape the at-rule needs: a dashed name for `@property`, a valid name for `@keyframes` and `@counter-style`, layer names for `@layer`, a URL for `@import`, nothing for `@font-face`.

**Why:** A browser drops an at-rule whose prelude is invalid, with everything inside it.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreAtRules` | `string[]` | `["media"]` | at-rules not to check; `@media` is left to `css/media-query-no-invalid` |

### How to fix

1. Rewrite the prelude in the form the at-rule's specification gives.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@property size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Do

```css
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@property size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Checks `@property`, `@font-palette-values`, `@position-try`, `@counter-style`, `@keyframes`, `@layer`, `@import`, `@namespace`, `@charset` and the at-rules that take no prelude; `@supports`, `@container`, `@page` and `@scope` preludes are not checked, as stylelint checks them with the CSSTree grammar codelaw does not ship.

## `css/block-no-redundant-nested-style-rules` — No `& { … }` wrapper

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (declarations moved out of the wrapper change place relative to the nested rules around it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/block-no-redundant-nested-style-rules.md

### What it checks

A nested style rule whose selector is only `&` is not used: its declarations go straight in the parent block.

**Why:** `& { … }` selects the same elements as its parent, so the wrapper only adds nesting.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  & {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  & {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/color-function-alias-notation` — `rgb()` and `hsl()`, not `rgba()` and `hsla()`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (browsers before 2018 ignore an alpha channel in `rgb()`)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/color-function-alias-notation.md

### What it checks

Colours use `rgb()` and `hsl()`; their aliases `rgba()` and `hsla()` are not used.

**Why:** The aliases are exactly equivalent today; one spelling is easier to search and read.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: rgba(0 0 0 / 50%);
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: rgb(0 0 0 / 50%);
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  color: rgba(0 0 0 / 50%);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: rgb(0 0 0 / 50%);
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `without-alpha`.

## `css/color-function-notation` — Space-separated colour functions

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (browsers before 2018 understand only the comma syntax)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/color-function-notation.md

### What it checks

`rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsl()` and `hsla()` use the modern space-separated syntax, with ` / ` before the alpha, not commas.

**Why:** The modern syntax is the one newer colour functions (`lab()`, `oklch()`) share.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: rgb(0, 0, 0);
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: rgb(0 0 0);
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  color: rgb(0, 0, 0);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: rgb(0 0 0);
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `modern`; values with `var()` inside are skipped.

## `css/container-name-pattern` — Container names are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every use of the name)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/container-name-pattern.md

### What it checks

Names given in `container-name`, `container` and `@container` match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent naming scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^(--)?([a-z][a-z0-9]*)(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression names must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the container to match the pattern.
2. Update every `@container` query that uses it.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
.card {
  container-name: cardGrid;
}
```

##### Do

```css
.card {
  container-name: card-grid;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.card {
  container-name: cardGrid;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.card {
  container-name: card-grid;
}
```

## `css/custom-media-pattern` — Custom media names are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every use of the name)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/custom-media-pattern.md

### What it checks

The name of each `@custom-media` (after `--`) matches a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent naming scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^([a-z][a-z0-9]*)(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression names must match (without the leading `--`) |

### How to fix

1. Rename the custom media to match the pattern.
2. Update every query that uses it.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@custom-media --smallViewport (width <= 30em);
```

##### Do

```css
@custom-media --small-viewport (width <= 30em);
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@custom-media --smallViewport (width <= 30em);
```

##### Do

```scss
@custom-media --small-viewport (width <= 30em);
```

## `css/custom-property-no-missing-var-function` — Custom properties are read with `var()`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (wrapping in `var()` makes a dropped declaration apply, which changes the page)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/custom-property-no-missing-var-function.md

### What it checks

A value names a custom property defined in the same sheet only inside `var()`.

**Why:** Without `var()` the value is the identifier `--name`, which is invalid for most properties, so the declaration is dropped.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
:root {
  --brand: red;
}

a {
  color: --brand;
}
```

##### Do

```css
:root {
  --brand: red;
}

a {
  color: var(--brand);
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
:root {
  --brand: red;
}

a {
  color: --brand;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
:root {
  --brand: red;
}

a {
  color: var(--brand);
}
```

## `css/custom-property-pattern` — Custom property names are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every use of the name, also in scripts)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/custom-property-pattern.md

### What it checks

Custom property names (after `--`), in declarations, `var()` and `@property`, match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent naming scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^([a-z][a-z0-9]*)(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression names must match (without the leading `--`) |

### How to fix

1. Rename the custom property to match the pattern.
2. Update every `var()` and script that reads it.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
:root {
  --brandColor: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
:root {
  --brand-color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
:root {
  --brandColor: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
:root {
  --brand-color: red;
}
```

## `css/declaration-block-no-duplicate-custom-properties` — No custom property declared twice in one block

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (which value should win can't be known from the code)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/declaration-block-no-duplicate-custom-properties.md

### What it checks

A declaration block declares each custom property once.

**Why:** Only the last declaration counts, so the earlier one is dead code or a mistake.

### How to fix

1. Decide which value the custom property should have.
2. Remove the other declaration.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  --gap: 4px;
  --gap: 8px;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  --gap: 8px;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  --gap: 4px;
  --gap: 8px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  --gap: 8px;
}
```

## `css/declaration-block-no-duplicate-properties` — No property declared twice in one block

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the earlier declaration may be a deliberate fallback for browsers that reject the later value)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/declaration-block-no-duplicate-properties.md

### What it checks

A declaration block declares each property once. Back-to-back declarations whose values have different syntaxes — a fallback such as `width: 100px; width: 50vw;` — are allowed, and so is `src`.

**Why:** The later declaration overrides the earlier one, so the earlier one is dead code or a mistake.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `["consecutive-duplicates-with-different-syntaxes"]` | `consecutive-duplicates-with-different-syntaxes` allows fallbacks |
| `ignoreProperties` | `string[]` | `[]` | properties to skip; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: pink;
  background: orange;
  color: orange;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  background: orange;
  color: orange;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  color: pink;
  background: orange;
  color: orange;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  background: orange;
  color: orange;
}
```

## `css/declaration-block-no-redundant-longhand-properties` — Shorthands instead of complete sets of longhands

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (combining longhands into a shorthand value needs the shorthand's grammar)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/declaration-block-no-redundant-longhand-properties.md

### What it checks

A block does not declare every longhand of a shorthand (`margin-top`, `margin-right`, `margin-bottom`, `margin-left`) where the shorthand would do, nor repeat a shorthand's value in one of its longhands.

**Why:** One shorthand is shorter and says plainly that every side is set.

### How to fix

1. Replace the longhands with the shorthand, giving their values in the shorthand's order.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  margin-top: 1px;
  margin-right: 2px;
  margin-bottom: 3px;
  margin-left: 4px;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  margin: 1px 2px 3px 4px;
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  margin-top: 1px;
  margin-right: 2px;
  margin-bottom: 3px;
  margin-left: 4px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  margin: 1px 2px 3px 4px;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Reported without a fix; stylelint rewrites some sets into the shorthand.

## `css/declaration-block-no-shorthand-property-overrides` — No shorthand after a longhand it resets

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (which value is meant can't be known from the code)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/declaration-block-no-shorthand-property-overrides.md

### What it checks

A shorthand property does not follow, in the same block, a longhand it covers.

**Why:** The shorthand resets the longhand declared before it, so the longhand never applies.

### How to fix

1. Move the longhand after the shorthand, or fold its value into the shorthand.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  padding-left: 10px;
  padding: 20px;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  padding: 20px;
  padding-left: 10px;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  padding-left: 10px;
  padding: 20px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  padding: 20px;
  padding-left: 10px;
}
```

## `css/declaration-property-value-keyword-no-deprecated` — No deprecated keywords in property values

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the replacement keyword is the closest modern one, not always identical)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/declaration-property-value-keyword-no-deprecated.md

### What it checks

Values use no keyword the specifications deprecated, such as `overflow: overlay`, `word-break: break-word` or the old system colours (`ThreeDFace`).

**Why:** Deprecated keywords are aliased or dropped by browsers and may stop working.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreKeywords` | `string[]` | `[]` | keywords to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  overflow: overlay;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  overflow: auto;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  overflow: overlay;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  overflow: auto;
}
```

## `css/declaration-property-value-no-unknown` — Keyword-valued properties use a known keyword

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended value is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/declaration-property-value-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

A property whose value is one keyword from a fixed set — `position`, `display`-like `float` and `clear`, `visibility`, `box-sizing`, `overflow`, border styles and others — is given one of those keywords or a CSS-wide keyword.

**Why:** The browser drops a declaration whose value it does not recognise.

### How to fix

1. Replace the value with one the property accepts.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  position: centre;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  position: relative;
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  position: centre;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  position: relative;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Checks single-keyword values of about forty keyword-valued properties, from a table written for this pack; stylelint validates every value against the full CSSTree grammar, whose data derives from MDN data (CC0), which codelaw does not ship.

## `css/font-family-no-duplicate-names` — No font family listed twice

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/font-family-no-duplicate-names.md

### What it checks

A `font-family` list (or the family part of `font`) names each family once. A quoted `"serif"` is a family name, not the `serif` keyword, so the two are different.

**Why:** The second mention can never be used, and usually hides a typo.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  font-family: Arial, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  font-family: Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif;
}
```

## `css/font-family-no-missing-generic-family-keyword` — Font lists end with a generic family

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (which generic family suits the fonts is a design call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/font-family-no-missing-generic-family-keyword.md

### What it checks

A `font-family` list (or the family part of `font`) includes a generic family such as `sans-serif`, `serif` or `monospace`. `@font-face`, values using `var()` and system fonts (`font: caption`) are skipped.

**Why:** When none of the named fonts is available the browser falls back to its default font, which may look nothing like the design.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreFontFamilies` | `string[]` | `[]` | families that need no generic fallback, such as icon fonts |

### How to fix

1. Add the generic family closest to the listed fonts at the end of the list.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  font-family: Helvetica, Arial;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  font-family: Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  font-family: Helvetica, Arial;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  font-family: Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif;
}
```

## `css/function-calc-no-unspaced-operator` — Spaces around `+` and `-` in math functions

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the fix makes an invalid, dropped declaration apply, which changes the page)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/function-calc-no-unspaced-operator.md

### What it checks

Inside `calc()` and the other math functions, `+` and `-` have whitespace on both sides.

**Why:** Without the spaces `-10px` reads as a negative number and `100%-10px` as one token, so the expression is invalid and the declaration is dropped.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  width: calc(100%-10px);
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  width: calc(100% - 10px);
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  width: calc(100%-10px);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  width: calc(100% - 10px);
}
```

### Differences from the source

Whitespace other than a single space around an operator is left to the formatter.

## `css/hue-degree-notation` — Hues are angles

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/hue-degree-notation.md

### What it checks

The hue of `hsl()`, `hwb()`, `lch()` and `oklch()` is written as an angle (`120deg`), not a bare number.

**Why:** An explicit unit makes the value's meaning plain.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: hsl(120 60% 50%);
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: hsl(120deg 60% 50%);
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  color: hsl(120 60% 50%);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: hsl(120deg 60% 50%);
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `angle`.

## `css/import-notation` — `@import` with `url()`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/import-notation.md

### What it checks

`@import` names its stylesheet with `url()`, not a bare string.

**Why:** One notation for imports is easier to search and read.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@import "theme.css";
```

##### Do

```css
@import url("theme.css");
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `url`.

## `css/keyframe-block-no-duplicate-selectors` — No keyframe selector twice in one `@keyframes`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (which keyframe was meant can't be known from the code)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/keyframe-block-no-duplicate-selectors.md

### What it checks

A `@keyframes` block names each keyframe selector once.

**Why:** Two blocks for one keyframe merge silently, which is usually a copy-paste slip.

### How to fix

1. Merge the two blocks, or change one selector to the keyframe it was meant for.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@keyframes fade {
  0% {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  0% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@keyframes fade {
  0% {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  100% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@keyframes fade {
  0% {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  0% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@keyframes fade {
  0% {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  100% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

## `css/keyframe-declaration-no-important` — No `!important` in keyframes

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (removing `!important` makes an ignored declaration apply, which changes the animation)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/keyframe-declaration-no-important.md

### What it checks

No declaration inside a `@keyframes` block is marked `!important`.

**Why:** Browsers ignore a keyframe declaration marked `!important`, so the property is not animated.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0 !important;
  }

  to {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  to {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0 !important;
  }

  to {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  to {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

## `css/keyframe-selector-notation` — Percentages for keyframe selectors

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/keyframe-selector-notation.md

### What it checks

Keyframe selectors are percentages (`0%`, `100%`) unless every selector of the `@keyframes` is a keyword (`from`, `to`).

**Why:** Mixing `from` with `50%` makes the timeline harder to read.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  50% {
    opacity: 0.5;
  }

  to {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@keyframes fade {
  0% {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  50% {
    opacity: 0.5;
  }

  100% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@keyframes fade {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  50% {
    opacity: 0.5;
  }

  to {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@keyframes fade {
  0% {
    opacity: 0;
  }

  50% {
    opacity: 0.5;
  }

  100% {
    opacity: 1;
  }
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `percentage-unless-within-keyword-only-block`.

## `css/keyframes-name-pattern` — Keyframes names are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every `animation` that uses the name)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/keyframes-name-pattern.md

### What it checks

The name of each `@keyframes` matches a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent naming scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^([a-z][a-z0-9]*)(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression names must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the keyframes to match the pattern.
2. Update every `animation` and `animation-name` that uses it.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@keyframes fadeIn {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@keyframes fade-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@keyframes fadeIn {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@keyframes fade-in {
  from {
    opacity: 0;
  }
}
```

## `css/layer-name-pattern` — Layer names are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every use of the layer)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/layer-name-pattern.md

### What it checks

Cascade layer names, in `@layer` and in `@import … layer()`, match a pattern: kebab-case segments joined by dots, by default.

**Why:** A consistent naming scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^([a-z][a-z0-9]*)([.-][a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression names must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the layer to match the pattern.
2. Update every `@layer` and `@import` that names it.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@layer baseStyles;
```

##### Do

```css
@layer base-styles;
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@layer baseStyles;
```

##### Do

```scss
@layer base-styles;
```

## `css/length-zero-no-unit` — No units on zero lengths

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/length-zero-no-unit.md

### What it checks

A zero length is written `0`, without a unit. Custom properties, `line-height`, `flex`, the line height in `font`, math functions and `fr` are skipped, as a unit matters there.

**Why:** `0px`, `0em` and `0` are the same length; the unit is noise.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `["custom-properties"]` | `custom-properties` skips custom property values |

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  margin: 0px;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  margin: 0;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  margin: 0px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  margin: 0;
}
```

## `css/lightness-notation` — Lightness is a percentage

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/lightness-notation.md

### What it checks

The lightness of `lab()`, `lch()`, `oklab()` and `oklch()` is written as a percentage.

**Why:** The functions use different number scales for lightness (0–1 and 0–100); a percentage reads the same in all of them.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: oklch(0.7 0.1 200deg);
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: oklch(70% 0.1 200deg);
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  color: oklch(0.7 0.1 200deg);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: oklch(70% 0.1 200deg);
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `percentage`.

## `css/max-lines` — A stylesheet stays under a line limit

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (splitting a stylesheet changes its structure and the order of the cascade)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/size` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/max-lines.md

### What it checks

A stylesheet has at most `max` lines (300 by default). It applies to whole
files only: `.css`, `.scss` and CSS Module files, never a `<style>` element
in a page.

**Why:** A very long stylesheet mixes concerns, is slow to read and review,
and makes it hard to see which rule wins. Neither stylelint nor Biome has a
rule for it, so these defaults are codelaw's own. The `css/size` preset turns
it on; give partials their own limit with a scope (for example `files =
["**/_*.scss"]` at 150).

A line holding code and a comment counts as code. The finding is reported
once, on the first line over the limit: "412 lines (max 300; blank lines and
comments not counted)".

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | `integer` | `300` | the most lines a stylesheet may have |
| `skip_blank_lines` | `boolean` | `true` | blank lines do not count |
| `skip_comments` | `boolean` | `true` | comment-only lines do not count: `/* */` and, in SCSS, `//` |
| `skip_imports` | `boolean` | `false` | `@import`, `@use` and `@forward` lines do not count |

### How to fix

1. Split the stylesheet by component or by concern: one file per component, or
   `base`, `layout`, `components`, `utilities`.
2. In SCSS, move each part to a partial (`_buttons.scss`) and pull it in with
   `@use`; with CSS Modules, one module per component.
3. Keep the order the cascade needs: import the parts in the order they had in
   the original file.
4. If the limit is wrong for these files, raise it for them with a `[scope]`
   table rather than for the project.

### Examples

## `css/media-feature-name-no-unknown` — No unknown media features

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended feature is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/media-feature-name-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Every media feature in `@media` and `@custom-media` is one the Media Queries specifications define. Vendor-prefixed features and custom media (`(--name)`) are skipped.

**Why:** A media feature the browser does not know never matches, so the block never applies.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreMediaFeatureNames` | `string[]` | `[]` | features to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### How to fix

1. Correct the feature name.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@media (min-widht: 600px) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@media (min-width: 600px) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@media (min-widht: 600px) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@media (min-width: 600px) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

## `css/media-feature-name-no-vendor-prefix` — No vendor-prefixed media features

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the value needs converting to a `dppx` resolution)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/media-feature-name-no-vendor-prefix.md

### What it checks

Media queries use no vendor-prefixed `device-pixel-ratio` feature.

**Why:** The standard `resolution` feature covers it in every current browser.

### How to fix

1. Replace the feature with `min-resolution`, `max-resolution` or `resolution`, and its value `n` with `ndppx`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@media (-webkit-min-device-pixel-ratio: 2) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@media (min-resolution: 2dppx) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@media (-webkit-min-device-pixel-ratio: 2) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@media (min-resolution: 2dppx) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

### Differences from the source

Reported without a fix: stylelint only drops the prefix, which leaves a non-standard feature.

## `css/media-feature-name-value-no-unknown` — Media features have valid values

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended value is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/media-feature-name-value-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

A media feature with a fixed set of values (`orientation`, `hover`, `prefers-color-scheme`, …) uses one of them, and a feature with a typed value (`width`, `resolution`, `color`) uses that type.

**Why:** A media query with an invalid value never matches, so the block never applies.

### How to fix

1. Use a value the media feature accepts.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@media (orientation: sideways) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@media (orientation: portrait) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@media (orientation: sideways) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@media (orientation: portrait) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

## `css/media-feature-range-notation` — Range syntax for media features

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/media-feature-range-notation.md

### What it checks

Range media features use the comparison syntax, `(width >= 600px)`, not `min-` and `max-` prefixes. The fix rewrites each prefixed feature on its own: `(min-NAME: V)` becomes `(NAME >= V)` and `(max-NAME: V)` becomes `(NAME <= V)`; a `min-` and `max-` pair becomes two ranges, which can be merged by hand into `(V1 <= NAME <= V2)`.

**Why:** Comparisons read like the condition they express, and can state exclusive bounds.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@media (min-width: 600px) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@media (width >= 600px) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `context`. The fix does not merge a `min-` and `max-` pair into one range.

## `css/media-query-no-invalid` — Media queries follow the grammar

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended query is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/media-query-no-invalid.md

### What it checks

Every query in `@media` and `@custom-media` is grammatical under Media Queries level 5: `not` is followed by a space, comparisons are `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=` or `=`, and `and` and `or` are not mixed without parentheses.

**Why:** A browser treats an invalid query as `not all`, so the block never applies.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreFunctions` | `string[]` | `[]` | functions to accept in queries, such as `theme` |

### How to fix

1. Rewrite the query; add parentheses to group `and` and `or`, and a space after `not`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@media (color) and (hover) or (width >= 600px) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@media (color) and ((hover) or (width >= 600px)) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@media (color) and (hover) or (width >= 600px) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@media (color) and ((hover) or (width >= 600px)) {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

## `css/media-type-no-deprecated` — No deprecated media types

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the media features that describe the device are the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/media-type-no-deprecated.md

### What it checks

Media queries use no media type the specifications deprecated: `tv`, `handheld`, `projection`, `aural`, `braille`, `embossed`, `speech` and `tty`.

**Why:** Deprecated media types match nothing, so the block never applies.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreMediaTypes` | `string[]` | `[]` | media types to accept |

### How to fix

1. Replace the media type with `screen`, `print` or `all`, adding media features that describe the device.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@media tv {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```css
@media screen {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@media tv {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@media screen {
  a {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

## `css/named-grid-areas-no-invalid` — Named grid areas are rectangles

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended layout is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/named-grid-areas-no-invalid.md

### What it checks

In `grid-template-areas` (and `grid-template`, `grid`), every row string has at least one cell, every row has the same number of cells, and each named area forms one filled-in rectangle.

**Why:** The browser drops an invalid `grid-template-areas` declaration, and the grid loses all its named areas.

### How to fix

1. Give every row the same number of cells.
2. Make each name cover a rectangle of cells.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  grid-template-areas:
    "head head"
    "side main main";
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  grid-template-areas:
    "head head head"
    "side main main";
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  grid-template-areas:
    "head head"
    "side main main";
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  grid-template-areas:
    "head head head"
    "side main main";
}
```

## `css/nesting-selector-no-missing-scoping-root` — Nesting selectors have a parent

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended parent selector is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/nesting-selector-no-missing-scoping-root.md

### What it checks

The nesting selector `&` is used only inside a style rule (or under `@scope`), where it stands for the parent selector.

**Why:** At the top level `&` matches the root element, which is almost never what was meant.

### How to fix

1. Nest the rule inside the rule `&` should refer to, or replace `&` with that selector.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
& .item {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
.list {
  & .item {
    color: red;
  }
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
& .item {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.list {
  & .item {
    color: red;
  }
}
```

## `css/no-descending-specificity` — Less specific selectors come first

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (reordering rules can change which declarations win)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-descending-specificity.md

### What it checks

A selector does not come after a more specific selector that targets the same element (the same last compound selector, pseudo-classes aside), within the same at-rule.

**Why:** The earlier, more specific rule wins whatever the order, so reading the sheet top to bottom misleads.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `[]` | `selectors-within-list` skips rules with a selector list |

### How to fix

1. Move the less specific rule above the more specific one.
2. Check that the page still renders the same.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
#nav a {
  color: red;
}

a {
  color: blue;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: blue;
}

#nav a {
  color: red;
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
#nav a {
  color: red;
}

a {
  color: blue;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: blue;
}

#nav a {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

A nested selector's `&` is resolved against each parent selector separately; stylelint uses the highest specificity among them, as `:is()` would.

## `css/no-duplicate-at-import-rules` — No stylesheet imported twice

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (removing the later import moves its rules earlier in the cascade)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-duplicate-at-import-rules.md

### What it checks

Each stylesheet is imported once with the same media conditions.

**Why:** The second import loads the same rules again, which costs a request and can reorder the cascade.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@import url("base.css");
@import url("base.css");
```

##### Do

```css
@import url("base.css");
```

## `css/no-duplicate-selector` — No selector declared twice

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (merging the rules depends on cascade order)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-duplicate-selector.md

### What it checks

Two rules in the same at-rule context do not have the same selector list (order and whitespace aside, nesting resolved), and one selector list does not name a selector twice.

**Why:** Split declarations for one selector are hard to follow and often contradict each other.

### How to fix

1. Merge the declarations of both rules into the first.
2. Check that rules between them did not depend on the order.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
.card {
  color: red;
}

.card {
  margin: 0;
}
```

##### Do

```css
.card {
  color: red;
  margin: 0;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.card {
  color: red;
}

.card {
  margin: 0;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.card {
  color: red;
  margin: 0;
}
```

## `css/no-empty-block` — No empty blocks

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-empty-block.md

### What it checks

No rule or at-rule has an empty block. A block holding only a comment is not empty, and `@layer name {}` is allowed because it fixes the layer's place in the cascade order.

**Why:** An empty block does nothing; it is usually left over from an edit or a placeholder that was never filled.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
.unused {}
a {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: red;
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.unused {}
a {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

`@layer name {}` is not reported: removing it would change the order of cascade layers.

## `css/no-empty-source` — No empty stylesheets

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to delete the file or fill it is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-empty-source.md

### What it checks

A stylesheet (or `<style>` element) holds something besides whitespace.

**Why:** An empty stylesheet is a wasted request or a file left behind.

### How to fix

1. Delete the file and what links it, or add the styles it was meant to hold.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css

```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss

```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/no-important` — No `!important`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the selector or layer that should win instead is a design call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/conventions` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-important.md

### What it checks

No declaration is marked `!important`.

**Why:** `!important` overrides the cascade, and the only way to override it is another `!important`, which escalates.

### How to fix

1. Find the rule `!important` was overriding.
2. Make this rule win by specificity, order or a cascade layer instead.
3. Remove `!important`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: red !important;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a.highlight {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  color: red !important;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a.highlight {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/no-invalid-double-slash-comments` — No `//` comments

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (turning it into a comment changes what applies)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-invalid-double-slash-comments.md

### What it checks

The sheet has no `//` comments: CSS has only `/* … */` comments.

**Why:** CSS reads `//` as part of a selector or property, so the rule or declaration after it is dropped.

### How to fix

1. Wrap the comment in `/* … */`, or delete it.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  // color: red;
  top: 0;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  /* color: red; */
  top: 0;
}
```

## `css/no-invalid-position-at-import-rule` — `@import` comes first

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (moving the import makes its rules apply, which changes the page)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-invalid-position-at-import-rule.md

### What it checks

Every `@import` comes before all other statements except `@charset` and `@layer` statements, and is not nested.

**Why:** Browsers ignore an `@import` that comes later, so the stylesheet is never loaded.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreAtRules` | `string[]` | `[]` | at-rules that may come before `@import` |

### How to fix

1. Move the `@import` to the top of the stylesheet.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  color: red;
}

@import url("theme.css");
```

##### Do

```css
@import url("theme.css");

a {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/no-invalid-position-declaration` — Declarations sit inside rules

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the selector it was meant for is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-invalid-position-declaration.md

### What it checks

A declaration sits inside a style rule, in an at-rule nested inside one, or in an at-rule that takes descriptors — never at the top level or directly inside a top-level `@media`.

**Why:** A declaration with no rule around it applies to nothing; the browser drops it.

### How to fix

1. Move the declaration into the style rule it belongs to.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
color: red;
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
color: red;
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/no-irregular-whitespace` — No irregular whitespace

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (replacing it changes which elements the selector matches)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-irregular-whitespace.md

### What it checks

Outside comments and strings, the sheet uses only ordinary whitespace: no no-break spaces, zero-width spaces or other Unicode spaces.

**Why:** An irregular space is part of the name around it, so `.menu .item` is one class name and the selector matches nothing.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
.menu .item {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
.menu .item {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.menu .item {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.menu .item {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/no-unknown-property` — No unknown properties

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the closest known name is a guess at what was meant)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/no-unknown-property.md

### What it checks

Every property is a known CSS property. Custom properties, vendor-prefixed properties and descriptors inside at-rules such as `@font-face` are skipped.

**Why:** The browser drops a declaration whose property it does not know, so a typo silently loses the style.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreProperties` | `string[]` | `[]` | properties to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |
| `checkPrefixed` | `boolean` | `false` | also check vendor-prefixed properties |

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  colr: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  color: red;
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  colr: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

The property table is `known-css-properties` plus the names stylelint keeps from before it moved to CSSTree, not CSSTree's MDN-derived data. A fix is offered when a known property is one or two edits away.

Numbers have at most four decimal places.

```css
  line-height: 1.333333;
```

##### Do

```css
  line-height: 1.3333;
```
```scss
}
```

## `css/selector-anb-no-unmatchable` — No An+B selector that matches nothing

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended position is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/selector-anb-no-unmatchable.md

### What it checks

`:nth-child()`, `:nth-of-type()` and their `last` forms are not given an argument that is always zero, such as `0`, `0n` or `0n+0`.

**Why:** Positions start at 1, so these selectors never match.

### How to fix

1. Use the position that was meant; the first element is `1`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
li:nth-child(0) {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
li:nth-child(1) {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
li:nth-child(0) {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
li:nth-child(1) {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/selector-class-pattern` — Class selectors are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update the markup and scripts that use the class)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/selector-class-pattern.md

### What it checks

Class names in selectors match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent naming scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^([a-z][a-z0-9]*)(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression names must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the class to match the pattern.
2. Update the markup and scripts that use it.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
.navBar {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
.nav-bar {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.navBar {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.nav-bar {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/selector-not-notation` — One `:not()` with a list

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the merged form has a lower specificity, which can change which rule wins)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/selector-not-notation.md

### What it checks

Adjacent `:not()` pseudo-classes are written as one `:not()` with a selector list: `:not(.a, .b)`.

**Why:** Selectors level 4 takes a list in `:not()`; one call reads more simply.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a:not(.active):not(.disabled) {
  color: gray;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a:not(.active, .disabled) {
  color: gray;
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a:not(.active):not(.disabled) {
  color: gray;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a:not(.active, .disabled) {
  color: gray;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `complex`.

## `css/selector-pseudo-class-no-unknown` — No unknown pseudo-classes

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended pseudo-class is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/selector-pseudo-class-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Every pseudo-class is one the specifications define, and pseudo-elements are written with `::`. Vendor-prefixed pseudo-classes are skipped; in `@page`, only page pseudo-classes are allowed.

**Why:** A browser drops a whole rule whose selector has a pseudo-class it does not know.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignorePseudoClasses` | `string[]` | `[]` | pseudo-classes to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### How to fix

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a:hovr {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a:hover {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a:hovr {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a:hover {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation` — Pseudo-elements with `::`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation.md

### What it checks

The pseudo-elements `::before`, `::after`, `::first-line` and `::first-letter` are written with two colons.

**Why:** Two colons tell pseudo-elements from pseudo-classes; the one-colon form exists only for CSS 2 compatibility.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a:before {
  content: "";
}
```

##### Do

```css
a::before {
  content: "";
}
```

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a:before {
  content: "";
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a::before {
  content: "";
}
```

### Differences from the source

Ported with stylelint-config-standard's setting, `double`.

## `css/selector-type-no-unknown` — No unknown type selectors

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS

### What it checks

Every type selector is an HTML, SVG or MathML element. Custom elements (a hyphenated lowercase name) are allowed by default, and namespaced selectors are skipped.

**Why:** A misspelt element name matches nothing.

### Options

| `ignore` | `string[]` | `["custom-elements"]` | `custom-elements` allows hyphenated names; `default-namespace` skips un-namespaced types |

```css
  border-collapse: collapse;
}
```
