```css
table {
  border-collapse: collapse;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
tabel {
  border-collapse: collapse;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
table {
  border-collapse: collapse;
}
```

## `css/shorthand-property-no-redundant-values` — No repeated values in shorthands

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/shorthand-property-no-redundant-values.md

### What it checks

Box shorthands such as `margin`, `padding`, `inset`, `gap` and `border-radius` give no value the shorthand would repeat anyway: `margin: 1px`, not `margin: 1px 1px`.

**Why:** The shorter form says the same thing.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  margin: 1px 1px;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  margin: 1px;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  margin: 1px 1px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  margin: 1px;
}
```

## `css/string-no-newline` — No line breaks inside selector strings

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the line break was meant is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/string-no-newline.md

### What it checks

A string in a selector does not contain an unescaped line break. With the default options, strings in at-rule preludes and declaration values are not checked.

**Why:** A raw line break ends a CSS string early, so the selector is invalid and the rule is dropped.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignore` | `string[]` | `["at-rule-preludes", "declaration-values"]` | contexts not to check: `at-rule-preludes`, `declaration-values` |

### How to fix

1. Join the string onto one line, or escape the line break as `\A`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
[title="one
two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```css
[title="one two"] {
  color: red;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
[title="one
two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
[title="one two"] {
  color: red;
}
```

## `css/syntax-string-no-invalid` — `@property` syntax strings are valid

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended type is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/syntax-string-no-invalid.md

### What it checks

The `syntax` of a `@property` rule is `"*"` or a `|`-separated list of supported `<type>` names and keywords, each with an optional `+` or `#`.

**Why:** A browser ignores a `@property` rule whose syntax is invalid, so the custom property is not registered.

### How to fix

1. Use a supported type name such as `<length>`, `<color>` or `<number>`.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
@property --size {
  syntax: "<size>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Do

```css
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@property --size {
  syntax: "<size>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@property --size {
  syntax: "<length>";
  inherits: false;
  initial-value: 0px;
}
```

## `css/value-no-vendor-prefix` — No vendor-prefixed values

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS, SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (browsers that need the prefix lose the value)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/standard` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/css/value-no-vendor-prefix.md

### What it checks

Values a build tool prefixes, such as `-webkit-flex` or `-moz-calc()`, are written without the prefix. `-webkit-box` and `-webkit-inline-box` are allowed, as line clamping still needs them.

**Why:** Prefixing is a build step; hand-written prefixes go stale and duplicate code.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreValues` | `string[]` | `["box", "inline-box"]` | values to accept, without their prefix; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css
a {
  display: -webkit-flex;
}
```

##### Do

```css
a {
  display: flex;
}
```
#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
a {
  display: -webkit-flex;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
a {
  display: flex;
}
```

## `data/outdated-dependency` — Dependencies are on their latest version

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-data` · `codelaw-rules-data` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a new major or minor version can change behaviour; the fix moves the range to the latest version, and the code that uses the package may need changes)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:data/package-json` at `warn` · `codelaw:data/pyproject` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/data/outdated-dependency.md

### What it checks

Each dependency of a `package.json` (`dependencies`, `devDependencies`, `peerDependencies`, `optionalDependencies`) and of a `pyproject.toml` (`[project] dependencies`, `[project.optional-dependencies]`, `[dependency-groups]`) is compared with `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, the registry facts `codelaw deps refresh` wrote. The rule reads only that file and the lockfiles; it never reads a registry, so `check` gives the same answer offline. With no snapshot, nothing is reported.

The version in use is the lockfile's (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `yarn.lock`, `uv.lock` or `poetry.lock`, beside the manifest or above it), else the one the range starts from. The latest is the highest stable version in the snapshot — by semver for npm, PEP 440 for Python — that is not deprecated or yanked and is at least `[deps] min_release_age` old on the snapshot's `fetched` date.

Each finding is graded, and `[deps] severity` sets each grade's severity (or `off`):

| finding | default |
|---|---|
| a major version behind | `warn` |
| a minor or patch version behind | `info` |
| the version in use is deprecated (npm) or yanked (PyPI) | `error` |
| the range already allows the latest, but the lockfile is behind | `info` |

The fix moves the range's version to the latest and keeps its operator: `^`, `~`, `>=`, `=` or none for npm; `==`, `>=` or `~=` for Python, at the precision written (`~=4.2` becomes `~=5.1`). A range the fix can't move without changing its meaning — `||`, a hyphen, `x`, an upper bound the latest is outside — is reported without a fix. `[deps] ignore` names packages never reported.

**Why:** A dependency left behind stops getting fixes and security patches, and the jump grows with every release; a deprecated or yanked version was withdrawn by its own maintainers.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw fix --unsafe` to move the range to the latest version, or edit the version by hand.
2. Run your package manager's install (`npm install`, `uv lock`, …) so the lockfile follows.
3. For a major version, read the package's changelog and update the code that uses it.
4. If the project must stay on this version, add the package to `[deps] ignore`, with an `expires` date when the stay is temporary.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-25",
  "packages": {
    "npm:react": { "latest": "19.2.0", "versions": { "18.3.1": "2024-04-26", "19.2.0": "2025-10-01" } }
  }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.1"
  }
}
```

##### Do

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-25",
  "packages": {
    "npm:react": { "latest": "19.2.0", "versions": { "18.3.1": "2024-04-26", "19.2.0": "2025-10-01" } }
  }
}
// package.json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "react": "^19.2.0"
  }
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-25",
  "packages": {
    "pypi:django": { "latest": "5.1.2", "versions": { "4.2.0": "2023-04-03", "5.1.2": "2024-10-08" } }
  }
}
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
dependencies = ["django~=4.2"]
```

##### Do

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{
  "fetched": "2026-10-25",
  "packages": {
    "pypi:django": { "latest": "5.1.2", "versions": { "4.2.0": "2023-04-03", "5.1.2": "2024-10-08" } }
  }
}
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
dependencies = ["django~=5.1"]
```

## `data/stale-deps-snapshot` — The dependency snapshot is recent

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-data` · `codelaw-rules-data` · **Languages:** JSON, TOML
- **Fix:** `manual` (refreshing the snapshot reads the registries, which needs the network; the engine never uses it (L5))
- **Severity when named:** `info` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:data/package-json` at `info` · `codelaw:data/pyproject` at `info`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/data/stale-deps-snapshot.md

### What it checks

`.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json` — the registry facts `data/outdated-dependency` reads — was fetched no more than `[deps] max_snapshot_age` (14 days by default) before the as-of date, and can be read. The finding is on the root `package.json`, or the root `pyproject.toml` when there is no root `package.json`, so a project gets one. The age is judged on the as-of date (`--as-of`, `CODELAW_AS_OF`, else `HEAD`'s commit date), never the clock; with no as-of date, only an unreadable snapshot is reported.

**Why:** An old snapshot hides every release since it was written, so `data/outdated-dependency` says a dependency is current when it isn't.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw deps refresh`: it reads npm and the Python index and writes the snapshot again.
2. Commit `.codelaw/deps-snapshot.json`, so CI and every teammate judge by the same facts.

### Examples

#### JSON

##### Don't

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": [ }
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
```

##### Do

```json
// .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": {} }
// package.json
{
  "name": "app"
}
```

#### TOML

##### Don't

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": [ }
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
```

##### Do

```toml
# .codelaw/deps-snapshot.json
{ "fetched": "2026-10-25", "packages": {} }
# pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "app"
```

## `graph/no-unused-css-classes` — CSS classes must be used somewhere

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-css` · `codelaw-rules-css` · **Languages:** CSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (A class can be built at run time or used by markup outside the repo, so removing its rule needs a human or agent to accept the diff.)
- **Severity when named:** `warn` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:css/project` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/graph/no-unused-css-classes.md

### What it checks

Every class a stylesheet defines appears in the project's HTML, JSX, templates or strings.

**Why:** a rule for a class no markup uses is dead weight every page downloads, and it makes the stylesheet harder to change safely.

### How to fix

1. Search for the class: a name built at run time (`"btn-" + kind`) counts only through its static prefix.
2. If markup outside the repo uses it, add the file to `[graph] keep` or list it in the package's `style` or `exports`.
3. Otherwise delete the rule, or the class from its selector list.

### Examples

#### CSS

##### Don't

```css files
/* src/styles.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
.legacy-banner { color: red; }
<!-- index.html -->
<div class="card"></div>
```

##### Do

```css files
/* src/styles.css */
.card { padding: 1rem; }
<!-- index.html -->
<div class="card"></div>
```

## `graph/no-unused-exports` — Exported symbols must be used somewhere

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-js` · `codelaw-rules-js` · `codelaw-rules-python` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX, Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (Static analysis can't rule out reflective or external use, so removal needs a human or agent to accept the diff.)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:js/project` at `error` · `codelaw:py/project` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/graph/no-unused-exports.md

### What it checks

Every exported symbol is imported by another module, is reachable from an entry point, or is marked `@public` / `@keep`.

**Why:** an export nothing imports is dead code that still looks like API: readers keep it, refactors carry it, and it hides what a module is really for.

### How to fix

1. Run `codelaw graph why-unused <symbol>` (`<file>#<export>` or `<module>:<name>`) to see each entry, keep and import clause.
2. If something outside the repo uses it, add the file to `[graph] entry` or `[graph] keep`, add its decorator to `[graph] registrars`, or tag it `/** @public */` / `# codelaw: keep`.
3. Otherwise delete the declaration (and its `__all__` or `export { … }` entry), or drop `export` if its own file still uses it.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js files
// src/date.js
export function formatDate(d) { return d.toISOString(); }
export function parseDate(s) { return new Date(s); }
// src/app.js
import { formatDate } from "./date";
console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

##### Do

```js files
// src/date.js
export function formatDate(d) { return d.toISOString(); }
// src/app.js
import { formatDate } from "./date";
console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx files
// src/Button.jsx
export function Button() { return <button />; }
export function Unused() { return <span />; }
// src/App.jsx
import { Button } from "./Button";
console.log(<Button />);
```

##### Do

```jsx files
// src/Button.jsx
export function Button() { return <button />; }
// src/App.jsx
import { Button } from "./Button";
console.log(<Button />);
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts files
// packages/utils/src/date.ts
export function formatDate(d: Date) { return d.toISOString(); }
export function parseDate(s: string) { return new Date(s); }
// packages/web/src/app.ts
import { formatDate } from "../../utils/src/date";
console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

##### Do

```ts files
// packages/utils/src/date.ts
export function formatDate(d: Date) { return d.toISOString(); }
// packages/web/src/app.ts
import { formatDate } from "../../utils/src/date";
console.log(formatDate(new Date()));
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx files
// src/theme.tsx
export const theme = { dark: false };
export const unusedTheme = { dark: true };
// src/main.tsx
import { theme } from "./theme";
console.log(theme);
```

##### Do

```tsx files
// src/theme.tsx
export const theme = { dark: false };
// src/main.tsx
import { theme } from "./theme";
console.log(theme);
```

#### Python

##### Don't

```py files
# app/dates.py
def format_date(d):
    return d.isoformat()
def parse_date(s):
    return s
# app/main.py
from app.dates import format_date
print(format_date(None))
```

##### Do

```py files
# app/dates.py
def format_date(d):
    return d.isoformat()
# app/main.py
from app.dates import format_date
print(format_date(None))
```

## `html/area-alt` — Image-map areas with a link have alt text

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the text that describes the area needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/area-alt.md

### What it checks

An `<area>` with `href` has non-empty `alt` text, and an `<area>` without `href` has no `alt`.

**Why:** A screen reader announces a linked area by its `alt`; without it the link has no name.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `accessible` | `boolean` | `true` | require `alt` on every linked area, not just one area per link target |

### How to fix

1. Give each linked `<area>` an `alt` that says where it leads.
2. Remove `alt` from an `<area>` that has no `href`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<img src="floor.png" usemap="#floor" alt="Floor plan">
<map name="floor">
  <area shape="rect" coords="0,0,50,50" href="/kitchen">
</map>
```

##### Do

```html
<img src="floor.png" usemap="#floor" alt="Floor plan">
<map name="floor">
  <area shape="rect" coords="0,0,50,50" href="/kitchen" alt="Kitchen">
</map>
```

## `html/aria-hidden-body` — <body> is not aria-hidden

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (removing it exposes the page to screen readers again, which changes what users hear)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/aria-hidden-body.md

### What it checks

`<body>` does not have `aria-hidden="true"`.

**Why:** It hides the whole page from assistive technology, while sighted users still see it.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<body aria-hidden="true">
  <p>Welcome</p>
</body>
```

##### Do

```html
<body>
  <p>Welcome</p>
</body>
```

## `html/aria-label-misuse` — aria-label is used only where it names something

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to move the label, add a role or use another element is a design decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/aria-label-misuse.md

### What it checks

`aria-label` and `aria-labelledby` appear only on elements that can carry an accessible name: interactive and labelable elements, landmarks, elements with a `role` or `tabindex`, and a few others (`img`, `table`, `fieldset`, `dialog`, …).

**Why:** On a plain `<span>` or `<div>` screen readers ignore the label, so the text never reaches the user.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowAnyNamable` | `boolean` | `false` | accept the label on any element ARIA lets be named, even where support is poor |

### How to fix

1. If the element acts as a control, use the matching element (`<button>`, `<a href>`) or add a `role`.
2. Otherwise put the text in the content, where everyone can read it, and remove the attribute.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<span aria-label="Close">×</span>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button" aria-label="Close">×</button>
```

## `html/attribute-allowed-values` — Attributes have values HTML allows

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended value can only be guessed)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/attribute-allowed-values.md

### What it checks

An attribute with a fixed set of values (`type`, `dir`, `loading`, …) uses one of them; a boolean attribute (`disabled`, `checked`) is written bare or with its own name; a numeric attribute holds a number.

**Why:** Browsers fall back to a default for a value they don't know, so a typo silently changes behaviour.

### How to fix

1. Check the attribute's allowed values (the message lists the one written).
2. Correct the value, or remove the attribute to get the default.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="emial" name="email">
<img src="a.png" alt="A" loading="later">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="email" name="email">
<img src="a.png" alt="A" loading="lazy">
```

## `html/attribute-misuse` — Attributes are used only where they take effect

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (either the attribute or its context is wrong, and only the author knows which)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/attribute-misuse.md

### What it checks

An attribute that only works in a given context is used there: `formaction` on a submit button, `target` on a link with `href`, `coords` with a `shape` that needs them, and similar.

**Why:** Outside that context the browser ignores the attribute, so the author's intent is lost.

### How to fix

1. Read the message: it names the attribute and what it needs.
2. Add the missing context (for example `href` or `type="submit"`), or remove the attribute.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<button type="button" formaction="/save">Save</button>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="submit" formaction="/save">Save</button>
```

## `html/autocomplete-password` — Password fields say which password they want

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the field asks for a new or the current password depends on the form)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/security` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/autocomplete-password.md

### What it checks

An `<input type="password">` has `autocomplete`, set to `new-password` or `current-password`, not `off`.

**Why:** Password managers autofill password fields anyway; saying which kind stops them filling a saved password into a "new password" field.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `preferred` | `string` | `""` | one value every password field must use, such as `current-password` |

### How to fix

1. Use `autocomplete="current-password"` on a sign-in form.
2. Use `autocomplete="new-password"` on a sign-up or change-password form.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="password" name="pw">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="password" name="pw" autocomplete="current-password">
```

## `html/button-type` — <button> says what type it is

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`type="button"` stops the button submitting its form; a button meant to submit needs `type="submit"` instead)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/button-type.md

### What it checks

A `<button>` has a `type` attribute (`button`, `submit` or `reset`).

**Why:** Without one a button submits its form, so a button meant to open a menu also sends the form, also when the user presses Enter.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<button>Open menu</button>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button">Open menu</button>
```

## `html/close-attr` — End tags have no attributes

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/close-attr.md

### What it checks

An end tag is just `</name>`, with no attributes.

**Why:** HTML ignores attributes on an end tag, so they are dead text that looks meaningful.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<p>Text</p class="intro">
```

##### Do

```html
<p>Text</p>
```

## `html/close-order` — Elements are closed, and in the order they were opened

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the missing end tag belongs depends on the intended structure)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/close-order.md

### What it checks

Every element whose end tag is required is closed, and no end tag closes an element that isn't open.

**Why:** Browsers repair mismatched tags by guessing, and the guess often nests content differently from what the author meant.

### How to fix

1. Find where the element named in the message should end.
2. Add its end tag there, or remove an end tag that closes nothing.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div>
  <span>Text
</div>
```

##### Do

```html
<div>
  <span>Text</span>
</div>
```

### Differences from the source

Elements whose end tag HTML lets you leave out (`<li>`, `<p>`, `<td>`, …) are not reported here; `html/no-implicit-close` reports them.

## `html/deprecated` — No obsolete elements

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the replacement — CSS, a semantic element, or nothing — depends on the intent)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/deprecated.md

### What it checks

The document uses no element HTML has made obsolete: `<center>`, `<font>`, `<marquee>`, `<frame>`, `<tt>` and the rest.

**Why:** Obsolete elements have no defined meaning, and some are rendered differently, or not at all, by current browsers.

### How to fix

1. Read the message for the usual replacement.
2. Use that element, or a class and CSS, instead.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<center>Welcome</center>
```

##### Do

```html
<div class="centered">Welcome</div>
```

## `html/doctype-html` — The doctype is the HTML5 one

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (switching to standards mode can change the page's layout)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/doctype-html.md

### What it checks

The doctype is `<!DOCTYPE html>`, not an HTML 4 or XHTML one.

**Why:** Legacy doctypes can put the browser in a quirks or "almost standards" mode, which lays pages out differently.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN" "http://www.w3.org/TR/html4/strict.dtd">
<p>Hello</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<p>Hello</p>
```

## `html/element-name` — Element names are HTML elements or valid custom elements

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming an element changes its CSS and script hooks)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/element-name.md

### What it checks

Every element is either an HTML element or a custom element whose name starts with a lowercase letter and contains a hyphen.

**Why:** An unknown element without a hyphen is a typo or an invalid custom element, and the browser treats it as an inline element with no meaning.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow` | `string[]` | `[]` | more element names to accept |

### How to fix

1. If the name is a typo of an HTML element, correct it.
2. If it is a custom element, give it a hyphenated name and rename its definition.
3. If a framework needs the name, add it to the `allow` option.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<widget>Hi</widget>
```

##### Do

```html
<x-widget>Hi</x-widget>
```

## `html/element-permitted-content` — Elements contain only content HTML allows there

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the right structure depends on what the markup is for)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/element-permitted-content.md

### What it checks

Each element contains only the elements its content model allows: no `<div>` inside a `<span>` or `<p>`, nothing interactive inside a link or button, no `<li>` directly inside a `<div>`.

**Why:** Browsers repair forbidden nesting by moving elements, so the DOM differs from the markup and styles and scripts miss.

### How to fix

1. Move the element named in the message out of the parent it can't be in.
2. Or change the parent to one that allows it (for example `<div>` instead of `<span>`).

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<p><div>Block</div></p>
<a href="/a"><button type="button">Go</button></a>
```

##### Do

```html
<div><p>Block</p></div>
<a href="/a">Go</a>
```

### Differences from the source

Obsolete elements (`<tt>`, `<font>`, `<acronym>`, …) have no content model in the element table, so html-validate reports them wherever they are; here they are left to `html/deprecated`, which reports each once.

## `html/element-permitted-occurrences` — Elements that may appear once do

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (which of the duplicates to keep is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/element-permitted-occurrences.md

### What it checks

Children that may appear only once in their parent do: one `<caption>`, `<thead>` and `<tfoot>` per table, one `<title>` and `<base>` per head, one `<legend>` per fieldset.

**Why:** The browser uses the first one and ignores the rest.

### How to fix

1. Merge the duplicates into one, or remove the extra one.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<table>
  <caption>Prices</caption>
  <caption>2024</caption>
  <tr><td>1</td></tr>
</table>
```

##### Do

```html
<table>
  <caption>Prices, 2024</caption>
  <tr><td>1</td></tr>
</table>
```

## `html/element-permitted-order` — Children come in the order HTML requires

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (moving markup may change how it is styled)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/element-permitted-order.md

### What it checks

Children with a required order are in it: in a table, `<caption>` then `<colgroup>`, `<thead>`, `<tbody>`/`<tr>`, `<tfoot>`; `<summary>` first in `<details>`; `<legend>` first in `<fieldset>`; `<source>` before `<img>` in `<picture>`.

**Why:** Out of order, browsers ignore or move the element, so it doesn't do its job.

### How to fix

1. Move the element named in the message before the one it must precede.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<details>
  <p>More text</p>
  <summary>Read more</summary>
</details>
```

##### Do

```html
<details>
  <summary>Read more</summary>
  <p>More text</p>
</details>
```

## `html/element-permitted-parent` — Elements have a parent HTML allows

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to wrap the element or change it depends on the intended structure)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/element-permitted-parent.md

### What it checks

Elements that need a particular parent have it: `<li>` in `<ul>`, `<ol>` or `<menu>`; `<title>` and `<base>` in `<head>`; `<head>` and `<body>` in `<html>`.

**Why:** Elsewhere they lose their meaning: an `<li>` outside a list is not a list item to assistive technology.

### How to fix

1. Wrap the element in the parent it needs.
2. Or replace it with an element that fits where it is.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div>
  <li>Apples</li>
</div>
```

##### Do

```html
<ul>
  <li>Apples</li>
</ul>
```

## `html/element-required-ancestor` — Elements are inside the ancestor they need

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to add the ancestor or use other elements depends on the intent)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/element-required-ancestor.md

### What it checks

Elements that only work inside a given ancestor are there: `<area>` in a `<map>`, `<dt>` and `<dd>` in a `<dl>`.

**Why:** Outside it they have no meaning and are rendered as plain text, or not at all.

### How to fix

1. Wrap the elements in the ancestor the message names.
2. Or replace them with elements that make sense where they are.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div>
  <dt>Term</dt>
  <dd>Definition</dd>
</div>
```

##### Do

```html
<dl>
  <dt>Term</dt>
  <dd>Definition</dd>
</dl>
```

## `html/element-required-attributes` — Elements have the attributes HTML requires

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the value can only come from the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/element-required-attributes.md

### What it checks

Elements have their required attributes: `src` on `<img>`, `lang` on `<html>`, `title` on `<iframe>`, `href` (or `imagesrcset`) on `<link>`, and so on.

**Why:** Without them the element does nothing useful: an `<img>` without `src` shows nothing, and an `<html>` without `lang` makes screen readers guess the language.

### How to fix

1. Add the attribute the message names, with the right value.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<html>
  <head><title>Home</title></head>
  <body><img alt="Logo"></body>
</html>
```

##### Do

```html
<html lang="en">
  <head><title>Home</title></head>
  <body><img src="logo.png" alt="Logo"></body>
</html>
```

## `html/element-required-content` — Elements contain the children HTML requires

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the content of the missing child needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/element-required-content.md

### What it checks

Elements that need a particular child have it: `<html>` has `<head>` and `<body>`, `<head>` has `<title>`, `<details>` has `<summary>`.

**Why:** A page without a `<title>` has no name in tabs, bookmarks and screen readers; a `<details>` without `<summary>` gets a generic label.

### How to fix

1. Add the child the message names, with real content.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
</head>
```

##### Do

```html
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <title>Pricing</title>
</head>
```

## `html/empty-heading` — Headings have text

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the heading text needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/empty-heading.md

### What it checks

Every `<h1>`–`<h6>` has text, or an image with `alt` text.

**Why:** Screen-reader users navigate by headings; an empty heading is a stop with nothing to announce.

### How to fix

1. Give the heading text, or remove it if it only made space (use CSS for that).

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<h2></h2>
<h2><span hidden>Pricing</span></h2>
```

##### Do

```html
<h2>Pricing</h2>
```

## `html/empty-title` — <title> has text

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the page title needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/empty-title.md

### What it checks

The `<title>` element has text.

**Why:** The title names the page in tabs, history, bookmarks, search results and screen readers.

### How to fix

1. Write a short title that says what the page is.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<title></title>
```

##### Do

```html
<title>Pricing — Acme</title>
```

## `html/fieldset-legend` — <fieldset> has a legend

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the group's name needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/fieldset-legend.md

### What it checks

A `<fieldset>` has a `<legend>` child.

**Why:** The legend names the group of controls; screen readers announce it with each control in the group.

### How to fix

1. Add a `<legend>` as the fieldset's first child, naming the group.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<fieldset>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label>
</fieldset>
```

##### Do

```html
<fieldset>
  <legend>Size</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label>
</fieldset>
```

## `html/form-dup-name` — Form controls have unique names

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming a control changes what the server receives)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/form-dup-name.md

### What it checks

Within a form, no two controls share a `name`, except radio buttons of one group, buttons, and a hidden default before a checkbox. A `name[]` array name is not mixed with the plain `name`.

**Why:** The server receives both values under one name and usually keeps only one of them.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowArrayBrackets` | `boolean` | `true` | let `name[]` repeat |
| `allowCheckboxDefault` | `boolean` | `true` | allow a hidden input before a checkbox of the same name |
| `shared` | `string[]` | `["radio", "button", "reset", "submit"]` | control types that may share a name |

### How to fix

1. Give each control its own name, and update the code that reads the form.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<form>
  <input type="text" name="email">
  <input type="email" name="email">
</form>
```

##### Do

```html
<form>
  <input type="text" name="name">
  <input type="email" name="email">
</form>
```

## `html/form-submit` — Forms have a submit button

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the button's label and placement need a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/form-submit.md

### What it checks

A `<form>` has a submit button, inside it or associated with it by `form=`.

**Why:** Without one there is no visible way to send the form; Enter-to-submit isn't obvious and doesn't work everywhere.

### How to fix

1. Add a `<button type="submit">` with a label that says what it does.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<form action="/search">
  <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search">
</form>
```

##### Do

```html
<form action="/search">
  <input type="search" name="q" aria-label="Search">
  <button type="submit">Search</button>
</form>
```

## `html/heading-level` — Headings start at <h1> and go down one level at a time

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (changing a heading level changes its style and the outline)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/document` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/heading-level.md

### What it checks

The first heading is `<h1>`, there is one `<h1>`, and each heading is at most one level below the one before it. A `<dialog>` starts its own outline.

**Why:** Screen-reader users navigate the heading outline; a skipped level looks like missing content.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowMultipleH1` | `boolean` | `false` | allow more than one `<h1>` |
| `minInitialRank` | `string` | `"h1"` | the lowest level the first heading may have (`h1`–`h6`, or `any`) |
| `sectioningRoots` | `string[]` | `["dialog", "[role=\"dialog\"]", "[role=\"alertdialog\"]"]` | selectors of elements that start their own outline |

### How to fix

1. Change the heading to the level the message expects, and restyle it with CSS if it looked right before.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<h1>Guide</h1>
<h3>Install</h3>
```

##### Do

```html
<h1>Guide</h1>
<h2>Install</h2>
```

## `html/hidden-focusable` — Focusable elements are not aria-hidden

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to unhide it, take it out of the tab order or remove it depends on the design)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/hidden-focusable.md

### What it checks

An element keyboard focus can reach — a link, a form control, anything with `tabindex="0"` — is not `aria-hidden`, itself or through an ancestor.

**Why:** Keyboard users land on it while screen readers say nothing, so blind keyboard users reach a silent stop.

### How to fix

1. Remove `aria-hidden` if the element should be announced.
2. Otherwise take it out of the tab order with `tabindex="-1"`, or hide it from everyone with `hidden` or `inert`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<a href="/home" aria-hidden="true">Home</a>
```

##### Do

```html
<a href="/home" aria-hidden="true" tabindex="-1">Home</a>
```

## `html/img-alt` — <img> has alt text

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (only a human can describe the image, or decide it is decorative)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/img-alt.md

### What it checks

Every `<img>` has an `alt` attribute: a description, or `alt=""` for a purely decorative image.

**Why:** Screen readers read the file name of an image without `alt`; `alt` is also shown when the image fails to load.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowEmpty` | `boolean` | `true` | accept `alt=""` for decorative images |
| `alias` | `string[]` | `[]` | other attributes that count as alt text, such as a framework binding |

### How to fix

1. Describe what the image shows, or what it is for, in `alt`.
2. If the image is decorative, write `alt=""`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<img src="team.jpg">
```

##### Do

```html
<img src="team.jpg" alt="The team at the 2024 offsite">
<img src="divider.png" alt="">
```

## `html/img-title` — Decorative images have no title

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the image is decorative or informative is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/img-title.md

### What it checks

An `<img>` with empty `alt` has no `title`.

**Why:** `alt=""` marks the image as decorative, while a `title` suggests it carries information; screen readers handle the mix inconsistently.

### How to fix

1. If the image carries information, move the text from `title` to `alt`.
2. If it is decorative, remove the `title`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<img src="logo.png" alt="" title="Acme">
```

##### Do

```html
<img src="logo.png" alt="Acme">
```

## `html/input-attributes` — Input attributes fit the input type

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (scripts or attribute selectors may still read the attribute)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/input-attributes.md

### What it checks

An `<input>` has only attributes its `type` uses: no `accept` on a text field, no `placeholder` on a checkbox, no `min` on an email field.

**Why:** The browser ignores them, so they mislead readers about how the field behaves.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="text" name="photo" accept="image/png">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="text" name="photo">
```

## `html/input-image-alt` — Image buttons have alt text

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the text needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/input-image-alt.md

### What it checks

An `<input type="image">` has non-empty `alt` text.

**Why:** The `alt` is the button's only name for screen readers and when the image doesn't load.

### How to fix

1. Add `alt` saying what the button does.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="image" src="go.png">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="image" src="go.png" alt="Search">
```

## `html/input-missing-label` — Form controls have a label

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the label text needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/document` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/input-missing-label.md

### What it checks

Every visible `<input>`, `<select>` and `<textarea>` has a label: a `<label for>`, a wrapping `<label>`, `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`, with text.

**Why:** Without a label, screen readers announce the control as "edit text" with no hint of what to enter.

### How to fix

1. Add a `<label for>` with text, or wrap the control in a `<label>`.
2. If a visible label is impossible, add `aria-label`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="text" name="q">
```

##### Do

```html
<label for="q">Search</label>
<input type="text" id="q" name="q">
```

## `html/link-text` — Links have text

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the link text needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/link-text.md

### What it checks

A link with `href` has text that says where it goes: content, an image with `alt`, or `aria-label`.

**Why:** Screen readers announce a link by its text; without it the user hears only "link".

### How to fix

1. Give the link text, an image with `alt`, or an `aria-label`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<a href="/cart"><img src="cart.png" alt=""></a>
```

##### Do

```html
<a href="/cart"><img src="cart.png" alt="Cart"></a>
```

## `html/long-title` — Page titles are short

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (shortening a title needs a human)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/long-title.md

### What it checks

The `<title>` text is at most 70 characters.

**Why:** Search results and browser tabs cut long titles, often before the words that matter.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `maxlength` | `integer` | `70` | the longest title allowed, in characters |

### How to fix

1. Shorten the title to what identifies the page.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<title>Acme Corporation — Products, Services, Pricing, Support, Downloads and Contact Details</title>
```

##### Do

```html
<title>Pricing — Acme</title>
```

## `html/map-dup-name` — Image maps have unique names

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming a map means updating the `usemap` that points at it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/map-dup-name.md

### What it checks

No two `<map>` elements share a `name`.

**Why:** An image's `usemap` picks one by name, so the other map is unreachable.

### How to fix

1. Rename one map and the `usemap` attributes that refer to it.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<map name="nav"></map>
<map name="nav"></map>
```

##### Do

```html
<map name="nav"></map>
<map name="footer-nav"></map>
```

## `html/map-id-name` — A map's id and name match

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (which of the two names is right depends on what refers to the map)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/map-id-name.md

### What it checks

When a `<map>` has both `id` and `name`, they are the same.

**Why:** HTML requires them to match; tools that look maps up by `id` and browsers that use `name` would find different maps.

### How to fix

1. Make `id` and `name` equal, and update references to the one you changed.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<map id="nav" name="menu"></map>
```

##### Do

```html
<map id="nav" name="nav"></map>
```

## `html/max-lines` — A page stays under a line limit

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (splitting a page into partials or components changes its structure)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/size` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/max-lines.md

### What it checks

An HTML file has at most `max` lines (400 by default). It applies to whole
`.html` and `.htm` files only.

**Why:** A very long page is hard to read and review and usually holds parts
that want their own component, partial or include. Neither html-validate nor
HTMLHint has a rule for it, so these defaults are codelaw's own. The
`html/size` preset turns it on.

A line holding markup and a comment counts as markup. With `skip_embedded`,
only the lines wholly inside a `<script>` or `<style>` body are left out; the
tag lines count. The finding is reported once, on the first line over the
limit: "412 lines (max 400; blank lines and comments not counted)".

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | `integer` | `400` | the most lines a page or template may have |
| `skip_blank_lines` | `boolean` | `true` | blank lines do not count |
| `skip_comments` | `boolean` | `true` | comment-only lines do not count: `<!-- -->` |
| `skip_embedded` | `boolean` | `false` | lines inside `<script>` and `<style>` do not count (the JS and CSS rules check their content) |

### How to fix

1. Pull a self-contained part (header, footer, a card, a form) into a partial,
   include or component.
2. Move a large inline `<script>` or `<style>` into its own file and link it.
3. If the limit is wrong for these files, raise it for them with a `[scope]`
   table rather than for the project.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

A page of 401 lines, one over the default limit (the example is long on
purpose):

```html
<p>Line 1</p>
```

## `html/meta-refresh` — Meta refresh redirects at once

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (redirecting at once or removing the refresh changes the page's behaviour)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error` · `codelaw:html/security` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/meta-refresh.md

### What it checks

A `<meta http-equiv="refresh">` redirects immediately (`0;url=…`); it doesn't wait, and doesn't reload the page.

**Why:** A timed refresh moves on before slower readers and screen-reader users have finished; a reload without a URL repeats forever.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowLongDelay` | `boolean` | `false` | allow delays over 20 hours (72,000 seconds) |

### How to fix

1. Make the refresh instant with `0;url=…`.
2. Or replace it with a link the user follows when ready.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="5;url=/next">
```

##### Do

```html
<meta http-equiv="refresh" content="0;url=/next">
```

## `html/missing-doctype` — The document has a doctype

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (leaving quirks mode can change the page's layout)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/document` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/missing-doctype.md

### What it checks

A document starts with `<!DOCTYPE html>`.

**Why:** Without it browsers render in quirks mode, which lays the page out differently from the standard.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<html lang="en">
  <title>Home</title>
</html>
```

##### Do

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
  <title>Home</title>
</html>
```

### Differences from the source

Only files with an `<html>` element are checked: a fragment or template partial is not a document, and gets no doctype of its own.

## `html/multiple-labeled-controls` — A label labels one control

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (each control needs its own label text)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/multiple-labeled-controls.md

### What it checks

A `<label>` is associated with at most one control, by nesting or by `for`.

**Why:** A label names one control; assistive technology announces the others without the right name.

### How to fix

1. Give each control its own `<label>`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<label>Name <input type="text" name="first"> <input type="text" name="last"></label>
```

##### Do

```html
<label>First name <input type="text" name="first"></label>
<label>Last name <input type="text" name="last"></label>
```

## `html/no-abstract-role` — No abstract ARIA roles

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the concrete role depends on what the element is)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-abstract-role.md

### What it checks

`role` does not name one of ARIA's abstract roles (`widget`, `input`, `landmark`, `section`, `command`, …).

**Why:** Abstract roles only organise the ARIA specification; browsers don't map them, so the element gets no role at all.

### How to fix

1. Use the concrete role that describes the element, or a native element.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div role="landmark">News</div>
```

##### Do

```html
<div role="region" aria-label="News">News</div>
```

## `html/no-autoplay` — Media does not play by itself

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the media no longer starts on load)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-autoplay.md

### What it checks

`<audio>` and `<video>` don't have `autoplay`.

**Why:** Sound that starts by itself talks over screen readers and startles users; WCAG asks that users control playback.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `include` | `string[]` | `["audio", "video"]` | elements on which `autoplay` is reported |

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<video src="intro.mp4" autoplay controls></video>
```

##### Do

```html
<video src="intro.mp4" controls></video>
```

## `html/no-conditional-comment` — No Internet Explorer conditional comments

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the markup inside is still needed is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-conditional-comment.md

### What it checks

The document has no conditional comments (`<!--[if IE]>…<![endif]-->`).

**Why:** Only Internet Explorer 9 and older read them; every current browser treats them as comments, so the markup inside is dead.

### How to fix

1. Delete the conditional comment, or move markup that is still needed out of it.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<!--[if lt IE 9]><script src="html5shiv.js"></script><![endif]-->
<p>Hello</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<p>Hello</p>
```

## `html/no-deprecated-attr` — No obsolete attributes

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the replacement is usually CSS, which needs a class and a rule)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-deprecated-attr.md

### What it checks

Elements don't use attributes HTML has made obsolete, such as `align`, `bgcolor`, `border` on `<img>`, or `name` on `<a>`.

**Why:** Browsers support them unevenly; CSS and current attributes do the same job reliably.

### How to fix

1. Replace presentational attributes with a class and CSS.
2. Replace other obsolete attributes with their current equivalent (for example `id` for `<a name>`).

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<img src="a.png" alt="Chart" align="left">
```

##### Do

```html
<img src="a.png" alt="Chart" class="float-left">
```

## `html/no-dup-attr` — No attribute written twice

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-dup-attr.md

### What it checks

An element does not have the same attribute twice (names compare without case).

**Why:** Browsers keep the first one and silently drop the rest, which is rarely what the author meant.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="text" name="q" name="search">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="text" name="q">
```

### Differences from the source

The fix removes the later copies, keeping what browsers already use. Check that the first value is the one you meant.

## `html/no-dup-class` — No class listed twice

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-dup-class.md

### What it checks

A `class` attribute lists each class once.

**Why:** The repeat does nothing, and suggests a merge went wrong.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<p class="lead lead">Text</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<p class="lead">Text</p>
```

## `html/no-duplicate-id` — Ids are unique in the document

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming an id breaks the CSS, scripts and links that use it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-duplicate-id.md

### What it checks

No two elements in the document have the same `id`. Ids inside a `<template>` only need to be unique within it.

**Why:** `getElementById`, `label for`, `aria-labelledby` and fragment links all find the first element with the id and miss the others.

### How to fix

1. Decide which element keeps the id.
2. Rename the other one, and update the CSS, scripts, `for`, `aria-*` and links that refer to it.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<h2 id="intro">Intro</h2>
<p id="intro">Text</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<h2 id="intro">Intro</h2>
<p id="intro-text">Text</p>
```

## `html/no-implicit-close` — Elements are closed explicitly

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the end tag goes after the element's last content, so whitespace that followed it moves outside the element)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-implicit-close.md

### What it checks

Elements whose end tag HTML lets you leave out (`<li>`, `<p>`, `<td>`, `<option>`, `<head>`, …) are closed with it anyway.

**Why:** Implied end tags make nesting hard to read, and an element closed by the next tag is easy to break when markup moves.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<ul>
  <li>One
  <li>Two
</ul>
```

##### Do

```html
<ul>
  <li>One</li>
  <li>Two</li>
</ul>
```

## `html/no-implicit-input-type` — <input> says what type it is

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`type="text"` is the default, but the field may have been meant as another type)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-implicit-input-type.md

### What it checks

An `<input>` has a `type` attribute.

**Why:** The default, `text`, is easy to leave by accident where `email`, `number` or `search` was meant.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input name="q">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="text" name="q">
```

## `html/no-inline-script` — No inline event handlers or javascript: URLs

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the handler has to move into a script file)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/conventions` at `error` · `codelaw:html/security` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-inline-script.md

### What it checks

Elements don't have inline event handlers (`onclick`, `onload`, …) or `javascript:` URLs.

**Why:** Inline script mixes behaviour into markup, can't be cached or tested, and is blocked by a strict Content Security Policy.

### How to fix

1. Give the element an id or class.
2. Attach the listener with `addEventListener` in a script file.
3. Replace a `javascript:` link with a `<button>`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<button type="button" onclick="save()">Save</button>
<a href="javascript:void(0)">Menu</a>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button" id="save">Save</button>
<button type="button" id="menu">Menu</button>
```

## `html/no-inline-style` — No inline styles

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the styles need a class and a stylesheet rule)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/conventions` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-inline-style.md

### What it checks

Elements don't have a `style` attribute, except one that only sets `display` or custom properties.

**Why:** Inline styles can't be reused, override stylesheets with high specificity, and are blocked by a strict Content Security Policy.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allowedProperties` | `string[]` | `["display"]` | properties an inline style may set |
| `allowVariables` | `boolean` | `true` | let inline styles set custom properties (`--name`) |

### How to fix

1. Move the declarations into a stylesheet rule for a class.
2. Replace the `style` attribute with that class.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<p style="color: red; font-weight: bold">Warning</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<p class="warning">Warning</p>
```

## `html/no-missing-references` — Id references point at an element

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (either the id or the reference is wrong, and only the author knows which)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/document` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-missing-references.md

### What it checks

Attributes that refer to ids — `for`, `form`, `list`, `headers`, `aria-labelledby`, `aria-describedby`, `aria-controls` and the others — name ids that exist in the document.

**Why:** A reference to a missing id silently does nothing: the label, description or relation is lost.

### How to fix

1. Correct the reference, or add the element it should point at.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="text" aria-describedby="hint">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="text" aria-describedby="hint">
<p id="hint">Use your work address.</p>
```

## `html/no-multiple-main` — One visible <main> per document

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (which one is the main content is a design decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-multiple-main.md

### What it checks

A document has at most one `<main>` without the `hidden` attribute.

**Why:** Assistive technology jumps to "the" main content; with two, users land on one and miss the other.

### How to fix

1. Keep one `<main>`; make the others `<section>`, `<aside>` or similar, or hide inactive ones with `hidden`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<main>Feed</main>
<main>Sidebar</main>
```

##### Do

```html
<main>Feed</main>
<aside>Sidebar</aside>
```

## `html/no-raw-characters` — Special characters are escaped

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-raw-characters.md

### What it checks

Text doesn't contain a raw `<` or an `&` that could be read as a character reference, and an unquoted attribute value doesn't contain `"`, `'`, `<`, `=`, `>`, `` ` `` or such an `&`.

**Why:** The parser can read them as markup: `&copy=1` becomes `©=1`, and `<` may start a tag.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `relaxed` | `boolean` | `false` | don't report `&` |

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<p>Fish & chips</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<p>Fish &amp; chips</p>
```

## `html/no-redundant-aria-label` — aria-label doesn't repeat the label

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-redundant-aria-label.md

### What it checks

A form control doesn't have an `aria-label` equal to the text of its `<label for>`.

**Why:** The label already names the control; the copy drifts out of date when only the visible label is edited.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<label for="q">Search</label>
<input type="text" id="q" aria-label="Search">
```

##### Do

```html
<label for="q">Search</label>
<input type="text" id="q">
```

## `html/no-redundant-for` — A wrapping label has no for

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-redundant-for.md

### What it checks

A `<label>` that wraps its control doesn't also point at it with `for`.

**Why:** Wrapping already associates them; the `for` is one more id reference to keep in sync.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<label for="q">Search <input type="text" id="q"></label>
```

##### Do

```html
<label>Search <input type="text" id="q"></label>
```

## `html/no-redundant-role` — No role the element already has

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-redundant-role.md

### What it checks

An element's `role` is not the role it has anyway, such as `<ul role="list">`, `<button role="button">` or `<a href role="link">`.

**Why:** The attribute repeats the element and suggests the element was chosen for its looks.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<ul role="list">
  <li>One</li>
</ul>
```

##### Do

```html
<ul>
  <li>One</li>
</ul>
```

### Differences from the source

Some Safari versions drop the list role of a `<ul>` styled with `list-style: none`; `role="list"` is a known workaround. Turn the rule off for such lists.

## `html/no-utf8-bom` — No UTF-8 byte-order mark

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the mark is in the file's bytes, outside the text a fix can edit; the editor's encoding setting removes it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/no-utf8-bom.md

### What it checks

An HTML file doesn't start with a UTF-8 byte-order mark (`EF BB BF`).

**Why:** UTF-8 needs no byte-order mark. Served or concatenated, the mark can show up as stray characters, or break a server-side include or a `<!DOCTYPE>` that must come first.

### How to fix

1. Save the file as UTF-8 without a byte-order mark. In VS Code, click the encoding in the status bar, choose *Save with Encoding*, then *UTF-8*.
2. Or strip it from the command line: `sed -i '1s/^\xEF\xBB\xBF//' <file>` (GNU sed).

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
﻿<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en"><title>Home</title></html>
```

##### Do

```html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en"><title>Home</title></html>
```

### Differences from the source

Only the file itself is checked: an HTML region inside another file (a Markdown fence, a template) holds no byte-order mark of its own.

## `html/prefer-button` — Buttons are <button> elements

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the element changes, so CSS and scripts that select `input` need updating)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/prefer-button.md

### What it checks

Buttons are written as `<button>`, not `<input type="button">`, `submit`, `reset` or `image`.

**Why:** `<button>` can hold markup and is styled and labelled more consistently.

### How to fix

1. Replace the `<input>` with a `<button>` of the same type, moving `value` into the content.
2. Update the CSS selectors and scripts that targeted the input.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="submit" value="Send">
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="submit">Send</button>
```

## `html/prefer-native-element` — Native elements instead of ARIA roles

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (swapping the element changes its styles and scripts)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:html/a11y` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/prefer-native-element.md

### What it checks

An element doesn't take a role a native element provides, such as `role="button"` on a `<div>` or `role="navigation"` on a `<div>`.

**Why:** Native elements bring keyboard handling, focus and semantics for free; a role brings only the announcement.

### How to fix

1. Replace the element with the native one the message names.
2. Remove the `role` and any keyboard handling the native element now provides.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div role="button" tabindex="0">Save</div>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button">Save</button>
```

## `html/prefer-tbody` — Table rows are in <tbody>

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/prefer-tbody.md

### What it checks

A table's `<tr>` rows sit in a `<tbody>` (or `<thead>`/`<tfoot>`), not directly in `<table>`.

**Why:** Browsers insert the `<tbody>` anyway, so the markup doesn't match the DOM that CSS and scripts see.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<table>
  <tr><td>1</td></tr>
</table>
```

##### Do

```html
<table>
  <tbody><tr><td>1</td></tr></tbody>
</table>
```

### Differences from the source

The fix is offered when the rows are next to each other; rows separated by other elements are only reported.

## `html/require-sri` — Scripts and stylesheets carry an integrity hash

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the hash must be computed from the exact file served)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/document` at `error` · `codelaw:html/security` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/require-sri.md

### What it checks

Every `<script src>` and `<link rel="stylesheet">` (and `modulepreload`, and `preload` of a script or style) has an `integrity` attribute.

**Why:** Subresource Integrity makes the browser refuse a file that changed on the CDN or in transit.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target` | `string` | `"all"` | `all` checks every resource; `crossorigin` only those loaded from another origin |

### How to fix

1. Compute the file's hash, for example `openssl dgst -sha384 -binary lib.js | openssl base64 -A`.
2. Add `integrity="sha384-…"` and `crossorigin="anonymous"`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js"></script>
```

##### Do

```html
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js" integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
```

## `html/script-element` — <script> has an end tag

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the markup the open script swallowed starts being rendered)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/script-element.md

### What it checks

A `<script>` is closed with `</script>`, also when it has `src`; `<script … />` is not a closed script.

**Why:** HTML ignores the `/>`, so the browser reads everything up to the next `</script>` as script and the content in between disappears.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<script src="app.js" />
<p>Hello</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<script src="app.js"></script>
<p>Hello</p>
```

## `html/script-type` — No type on JavaScript scripts

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/script-type.md

### What it checks

A `<script>` doesn't say `type="text/javascript"` or another JavaScript MIME type.

**Why:** JavaScript is the default; the attribute adds nothing, and legacy types such as `text/ecmascript` mislead.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<script type="text/javascript" src="app.js"></script>
```

##### Do

```html
<script src="app.js"></script>
```

## `html/target-blank-rel` — Links that open a new tab set rel="noopener"

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-html` · `codelaw-rules-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:html/conventions` at `error` · `codelaw:html/security` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/html/target-blank-rel.md

### What it checks

An `<a>` or `<area>` with `target="_blank"` and an `href` (or a `<form>` with an `action`) has `rel="noopener"` or `rel="noreferrer"`.

**Why:** Without it, older browsers give the opened page a handle on this one (`window.opener`), which it can use to redirect it.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<a href="https://example.com" target="_blank">Example</a>
```

##### Do

```html
<a href="https://example.com" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Example</a>
```
