```ts
function useFilters() {
  const [filters, setFilters] = useState(() => ({ tags: readTags() }));
  return [filters, setFilters] as const;
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
function Editor() {
  const [doc] = useState(createDocument());
  return <article>{doc.title}</article>;
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
function Editor() {
  const [doc] = useState(() => createDocument());
  return <article>{doc.title}</article>;
}
```

### Differences from the source

- This is the lazy-initialisation part of @eslint-react's `use-state`; its other two checks — that the call is destructured, and that the setter is named `set` + the value's name — are naming conventions, not ported here.
- Upstream reports each call in the argument; codelaw reports the argument once, naming the first call, and offers one fix for it.

## `react/props-type-name` — A component's props type is named <Component>Props

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-react` · `codelaw-rules-react` · **Languages:** TSX
- **Fix:** `suggest` (renaming a type other files import would break them, so it is offered, not applied)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:react/conventions` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/react/props-type-name.md

### What it checks

The type of a component's props is named after the component: `CardProps` for `Card`.

**Why:** One naming pattern makes props types easy to find and import.

### Examples

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
type CardOptions = { title: string };
export function Card(props: CardOptions) {
  return <h2>{props.title}</h2>;
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
type CardProps = { title: string };
export function Card(props: CardProps) {
  return <h2>{props.title}</h2>;
}
```

### Differences from the source

The type is renamed with its uses in the file; an exported type is reported without a fix.

## `react/purity` — Render doesn't call Math.random(), Date.now() or other impure functions

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-react` · `codelaw-rules-react` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the value should come from instead — state, an effect, an event — depends on what it is for)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:react/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/react/purity.md

### What it checks

A component or hook doesn't call `Math.random()`, `Date.now()`, `performance.now()`,
`crypto.randomUUID()` or `crypto.getRandomValues()`, or make `new Date()` with no argument, in its
own body. Calls in callbacks — effects, event handlers, a `useState` initializer — are fine, and so
is a local binding that shadows the global (`Math` as a parameter).

**Why:** React may render a component any number of times and expects the same output for the same props and state; a value that changes on every call makes the output change on every render and breaks hydration.

### How to fix

1. For a value made once, compute it in a `useState` initializer: `useState(() => Date.now())`.
2. For an id, use `useId()`.
3. For a value that should change, set it in an effect or an event handler.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
function useRandomKey() {
  return Math.random().toString(36);
}
```

##### Do

```js
function useRandomKey() {
  const [key] = useState(() => Math.random().toString(36));
  return key;
}
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
function Clock() {
  const now = Date.now();
  return <p>{now}</p>;
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
function Clock() {
  const [now] = useState(() => Date.now());
  return <p>{now}</p>;
}
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
function useToday(): string {
  return new Date().toDateString();
}
```

##### Do

```ts
function useToday(): string {
  const [today] = useState(() => new Date().toDateString());
  return today;
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
function Field({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const id = crypto.randomUUID();
  return <label htmlFor={id}>{label}</label>;
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
function Field({ label }: { label: string }) {
  const id = useId();
  return <label htmlFor={id}>{label}</label>;
}
```

### Differences from the source

- eslint-plugin-react-hooks 7 knows `Math.random`, `Date.now` and `performance.now`; codelaw adds `crypto.randomUUID`, `crypto.getRandomValues` and `new Date()` from @eslint-react's list, and leaves out the rest of that list (DOM, storage, network and timer calls), which reads as side effects more than impurity and is better reported by a rule of its own.
- Upstream follows a global through an alias (`const { random } = Math`); codelaw reports only the direct `Math.random()` form.
- A call in a function the component calls during render is not followed.

## `react/require-render-return` — A class component's render() returns

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-react` · `codelaw-rules-react` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (what to render needs the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:react/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/react/require-render-return.md

### What it checks

The `render()` method of a class component returns a value on every path.

**Why:** A `render()` that falls off its end returns `undefined`, which is almost always a forgotten
`return`.

### How to fix

1. Return the element, or `null` to render nothing, on every path.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
class Title extends React.Component {
  render() {
    <h1>{this.props.text}</h1>;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```js
class Title extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <h1>{this.props.text}</h1>;
  }
}
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
class Title extends React.Component {
  render() {
    <h1>{this.props.text}</h1>;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
class Title extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <h1>{this.props.text}</h1>;
  }
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
class Title extends React.Component {
  render() {
    <h1>{this.props.text}</h1>;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
class Title extends React.Component {
  render() {
    return <h1>{this.props.text}</h1>;
  }
}
```

## `react/rules-of-hooks` — Hooks are called at the top level of components and hooks

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-react` · `codelaw-rules-react` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (moving a hook can change what the code does on the renders that skipped it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:react/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/react/rules-of-hooks.md

### What it checks

Hooks (`useState`, `useEffect`, any `use…`) are called only at the top level of a function component
or a custom hook: not in conditions, loops, nested functions, after an early return, in classes, or
in plain functions.

**Why:** React matches hook calls to state by their order, so a hook that runs on some renders and
not others mixes up every hook after it.

### How to fix

1. Move the hook call to the top level of the component or hook, before any early return.
2. Put the condition inside the hook (e.g. inside the effect) instead of around it.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
function Profile({ id }) {
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  const [user] = useState(null);
  return user;
}
```

##### Do

```js
function Profile({ id }) {
  const [user] = useState(null);
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  return user;
}
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
function Profile({ id }) {
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  const [user] = useState(null);
  return user;
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
function Profile({ id }) {
  const [user] = useState(null);
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  return user;
}
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
function useProfile(id: string) {
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  return useState(id);
}
```

##### Do

```ts
function useProfile(id: string) {
  const state = useState(id);
  return id ? state : null;
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
function Profile({ id }) {
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  const [user] = useState(null);
  return user;
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
function Profile({ id }) {
  const [user] = useState(null);
  if (!id) {
    return null;
  }
  return user;
}
```

## `react/use-memo` — useMemo's callback computes and returns a value

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-react` · `codelaw-rules-react` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the code belongs in useEffect, useCallback or plain render code is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:react/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/react/use-memo.md

### What it checks

`useMemo(fn, deps)`'s callback is a plain synchronous function with no parameters that returns a
value, and the call's result is used. Reported: an `async` or generator callback, a callback that
takes parameters, a callback with a block body and no `return` of a value, and a `useMemo(…)` call
whose result is thrown away.

**Why:** `useMemo` caches the value its callback returns, calling it with no arguments: an `async` callback caches a promise, a parameter is always `undefined`, and a callback that returns nothing is a side effect in render, which belongs in `useEffect`.

### How to fix

1. For a side effect, use `useEffect` instead.
2. For an async value, load it in an effect (or a data library) and keep it in state.
3. Read the values the callback needs from the component's scope instead of parameters, and return the result.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
function useTotal(items) {
  return useMemo(async () => sum(items), [items]);
}
```

##### Do

```js
function useTotal(items) {
  return useMemo(() => sum(items), [items]);
}
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
function Report({ rows }) {
  const sorted = useMemo(() => {
    rows.sort(byDate);
  }, [rows]);
  return <Table rows={sorted} />;
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
function Report({ rows }) {
  const sorted = useMemo(() => [...rows].sort(byDate), [rows]);
  return <Table rows={sorted} />;
}
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
function useLabel(id: string) {
  return useMemo((prefix: string) => prefix + id, [id]);
}
```

##### Do

```ts
function useLabel(id: string) {
  return useMemo(() => 'item-' + id, [id]);
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
function Log({ value }: { value: number }) {
  useMemo(() => console.log(value), [value]);
  return <p>{value}</p>;
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
function Log({ value }: { value: number }) {
  useEffect(() => console.log(value), [value]);
  return <p>{value}</p>;
}
```

### Differences from the source

- Upstream also reports a `useMemo` callback that reassigns a variable from outside it, and a callback given by name (`useMemo(fn, deps)`) rather than written in place; codelaw does neither.
- An unused result is reported only when the call is a statement of its own; upstream follows the value through the function.

## `redux-toolkit/no-blind-payload-return` — A reducer builds its state, not the action's payload

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the reducer has to name the fields it takes from the payload)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/no-blind-payload-return.md

### What it checks

A reducer doesn't return `action.payload` as the new state, return an object spreading
`...action.payload`, or `Object.assign` the payload onto an Immer draft.

**Why:** Whoever dispatches the action then decides the shape of the state, and a payload with a missing or
extra field changes it without the reducer knowing. *Style Guide, Priority B: Reducers Should Own the
State Shape.* The guide allows a spread for a form that edits every field; `redux-toolkit/recommended`
warns rather than errs.

### How to fix

1. Copy the fields the state owns from the payload by name: `state.name = action.payload.name`.
2. If replacing the whole state is the point (a cache reset), write that as its own case with a
   descriptive action name, and suppress the finding there.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const userSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'user',
  initialState: { name: '', email: '' },
  reducers: {
    userUpdated(state, action) {
      return action.payload;
    },
  },
});
```

##### Do

```js
const userSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'user',
  initialState: { name: '', email: '' },
  reducers: {
    userUpdated(state, action) {
      state.name = action.payload.name;
      state.email = action.payload.email;
    },
  },
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const userSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'user',
  initialState: { name: '', email: '' },
  reducers: {
    userUpdated(state, action) {
      return action.payload;
    },
  },
});
```

##### Do

```jsx
const userSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'user',
  initialState: { name: '', email: '' },
  reducers: {
    userUpdated(state, action) {
      state.name = action.payload.name;
      state.email = action.payload.email;
    },
  },
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const userSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'user',
  initialState: { name: '', email: '' },
  reducers: {
    userUpdated(state, action) {
      return action.payload;
    },
  },
});
```

##### Do

```ts
const userSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'user',
  initialState: { name: '', email: '' },
  reducers: {
    userUpdated(state, action) {
      state.name = action.payload.name;
      state.email = action.payload.email;
    },
  },
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const userSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'user',
  initialState: { name: '', email: '' },
  reducers: {
    userUpdated(state, action) {
      return action.payload;
    },
  },
});
```

##### Do

```tsx
const userSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'user',
  initialState: { name: '', email: '' },
  reducers: {
    userUpdated(state, action) {
      state.name = action.payload.name;
      state.email = action.payload.email;
    },
  },
});
```

## `redux-toolkit/no-immutable-js` — State is plain JavaScript, not Immutable.js

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (every read and update of the state is rewritten for plain objects)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/no-immutable-js.md

### What it checks

Nothing is imported from `immutable` (Immutable.js).

**Why:** Immutable.js values spread through the code that reads them, need conversion at every boundary and
don't serialize as plain data; Redux Toolkit's Immer gives immutable updates on plain objects. *Style
Guide, Priority B: Use Plain JavaScript Objects for State.*

### How to fix

1. Store the state as plain objects and arrays (`fromJS(x).toJS()` once, at the boundary).
2. Rewrite the reducers with `createSlice`, and the reads (`state.get('a')`) as property access.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
import { Map } from 'immutable';
```

##### Do

```js
import { createSlice } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
import { Map } from 'immutable';
```

##### Do

```jsx
import { createSlice } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
import { Map } from 'immutable';
```

##### Do

```ts
import { createSlice } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
import { Map } from 'immutable';
```

##### Do

```tsx
import { createSlice } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
```

## `redux-toolkit/no-legacy-create-store` — The store is made with configureStore

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (`configureStore` takes its options in another shape, and the middleware and enhancers move)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/no-legacy-create-store.md

### What it checks

`createStore` and `legacy_createStore` are not imported from `redux`; the store is made with Redux
Toolkit's `configureStore`.

**Why:** `configureStore` sets up the thunk middleware, the DevTools and the mutation and serializability
checks that catch the Priority A mistakes; `createStore` sets up none of them. *Style Guide, Priority
B: Use Redux Toolkit for Writing Redux Logic.*

### How to fix

1. Import `configureStore` from `@reduxjs/toolkit`.
2. Replace `createStore(rootReducer, preloadedState, enhancer)` with
   `configureStore({ reducer: rootReducer, preloadedState })`; pass extra middleware through
   `middleware: (getDefault) => getDefault().concat(…)`.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
import { createStore } from 'redux';
```

##### Do

```js
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
import { createStore } from 'redux';
```

##### Do

```jsx
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
import { createStore } from 'redux';
```

##### Do

```ts
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
import { createStore } from 'redux';
```

##### Do

```tsx
import { configureStore } from '@reduxjs/toolkit';
```

## `redux-toolkit/no-mutating-reducer` — A hand-written reducer doesn't change its state in place

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the update has to be rewritten to return a new value)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/no-mutating-reducer.md

### What it checks

A hand-written reducer — a function `(state, action)` that tests `action.type`, outside
`createSlice`, `createReducer` and `produce` — does not assign to, delete from, or call a mutating
method (`push`, `splice`, `sort`, `Object.assign(state, …)`, …) on its `state`.

**Why:** Redux compares state by reference: a state changed in place is the same object, so the UI doesn't
update, and time-travel debugging shows the wrong history. *Style Guide, Priority A: Do Not Mutate
State.* Inside `createSlice` the state is an Immer draft, and changing it is how updates are written.

### How to fix

1. Return a new value: `[...state, item]`, `{ ...state, field: value }`, `state.filter(…)`.
2. Better, rewrite the reducer with `createSlice`, where the in-place update is correct.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
function todos(state = [], action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'todos/added':
      state.push(action.payload);
      return state;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```js
function todos(state = [], action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'todos/added':
      return [...state, action.payload];
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
function todos(state = [], action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'todos/added':
      state.push(action.payload);
      return state;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
function todos(state = [], action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'todos/added':
      return [...state, action.payload];
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
function todos(state = [], action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'todos/added':
      state.push(action.payload);
      return state;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```ts
function todos(state = [], action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'todos/added':
      return [...state, action.payload];
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
function todos(state = [], action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'todos/added':
      state.push(action.payload);
      return state;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
function todos(state = [], action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'todos/added':
      return [...state, action.payload];
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

## `redux-toolkit/no-non-serializable-state` — State holds only serializable values

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the data has to be stored in another shape, and the code reading it changed)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/no-non-serializable-state.md

### What it checks

A slice's `initialState` (in `createSlice` or `createReducer`, followed through a `const`) and the
values a reducer assigns into its state are plain objects, arrays and primitives: no `Map`, `Set`,
`Date`, `Promise`, class instance, `Symbol`, function or regular expression.

**Why:** The DevTools, persistence and time-travel all serialize the state; a value that doesn't survive
`JSON.stringify` breaks them, and Redux Toolkit's serializability check warns at run time. *Style
Guide, Priority A: Do Not Put Non-Serializable Values in State or Actions.*

### How to fix

1. Store a `Map` or `Set` as an object keyed by ID, or as an array.
2. Store a `Date` as its ISO string or its timestamp, and make the `Date` where it is displayed.
3. Keep functions and class instances outside the store; store an ID that finds them.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const usersSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'users',
  initialState: { byId: new Map() },
  reducers: {},
});
```

##### Do

```js
const usersSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'users',
  initialState: { byId: {} },
  reducers: {},
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const usersSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'users',
  initialState: { byId: new Map() },
  reducers: {},
});
```

##### Do

```jsx
const usersSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'users',
  initialState: { byId: {} },
  reducers: {},
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const usersSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'users',
  initialState: { byId: new Map() },
  reducers: {},
});
```

##### Do

```ts
const usersSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'users',
  initialState: { byId: {} },
  reducers: {},
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const usersSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'users',
  initialState: { byId: new Map() },
  reducers: {},
});
```

##### Do

```tsx
const usersSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'users',
  initialState: { byId: {} },
  reducers: {},
});
```

## `redux-toolkit/no-object-selector` — useSelector selects one value per call

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the one call is split into one per value, and the destructuring goes)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/no-object-selector.md

### What it checks

A selector passed alone to `useSelector` (or a typed `use…Selector` hook) doesn't return a new object
literal.

**Why:** `useSelector` re-renders when the selected value changes by reference, and a new object is a new
reference after every dispatched action, so the component re-renders on all of them. *Style Guide,
Priority B: Call useSelector Multiple Times in Function Components.* An equality function such as
`shallowEqual` as the second argument avoids it, and is left alone.

### How to fix

1. Call `useSelector` once per value: `const todos = useSelector((state) => state.todos)`.
2. Or pass `shallowEqual` as the second argument when one object is really wanted.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
function TodoList() {
  const { todos, filter } = useSelector((state) => ({ todos: state.todos, filter: state.filter }));
  return [todos, filter];
}
```

##### Do

```js
function TodoList() {
  const todos = useSelector((state) => state.todos);
  const filter = useSelector((state) => state.filter);
  return [todos, filter];
}
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
function TodoList() {
  const { todos, filter } = useSelector((state) => ({ todos: state.todos, filter: state.filter }));
  return [todos, filter];
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
function TodoList() {
  const todos = useSelector((state) => state.todos);
  const filter = useSelector((state) => state.filter);
  return [todos, filter];
}
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
function TodoList() {
  const { todos, filter } = useSelector((state) => ({ todos: state.todos, filter: state.filter }));
  return [todos, filter];
}
```

##### Do

```ts
function TodoList() {
  const todos = useSelector((state) => state.todos);
  const filter = useSelector((state) => state.filter);
  return [todos, filter];
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
function TodoList() {
  const { todos, filter } = useSelector((state) => ({ todos: state.todos, filter: state.filter }));
  return [todos, filter];
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
function TodoList() {
  const todos = useSelector((state) => state.todos);
  const filter = useSelector((state) => state.filter);
  return [todos, filter];
}
```

## `redux-toolkit/no-sequential-dispatch` — One event is one action, not a run of dispatches

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the actions have to be merged into one that the reducers all respond to)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/no-sequential-dispatch.md

### What it checks

A block doesn't dispatch more than `max` (2) actions in a row, statement after statement.

**Why:** Each dispatch re-renders the subscribers and leaves the state halfway between the first action and
the last, a state no reducer meant. *Style Guide, Priority B: Avoid Dispatching Many Actions
Sequentially; Model Actions as Events, Not Setters.*

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | `integer` | `2` | how many `dispatch` statements in a row are accepted |

### How to fix

1. Dispatch one action that describes what happened (`orderPlaced`), with what the reducers need in
   its payload.
2. Let each slice that cares respond to it in `extraReducers`.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
function placeOrder(dispatch) {
  dispatch(setPizzas(1));
  dispatch(setCokes(1));
  dispatch(setTotal(12));
}
```

##### Do

```js
function placeOrder(dispatch) {
  dispatch(orderPlaced({ pizza: 1, coke: 1 }));
}
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
function placeOrder(dispatch) {
  dispatch(setPizzas(1));
  dispatch(setCokes(1));
  dispatch(setTotal(12));
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
function placeOrder(dispatch) {
  dispatch(orderPlaced({ pizza: 1, coke: 1 }));
}
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
function placeOrder(dispatch) {
  dispatch(setPizzas(1));
  dispatch(setCokes(1));
  dispatch(setTotal(12));
}
```

##### Do

```ts
function placeOrder(dispatch) {
  dispatch(orderPlaced({ pizza: 1, coke: 1 }));
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
function placeOrder(dispatch) {
  dispatch(setPizzas(1));
  dispatch(setCokes(1));
  dispatch(setTotal(12));
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
function placeOrder(dispatch) {
  dispatch(orderPlaced({ pizza: 1, coke: 1 }));
}
```

## `redux-toolkit/no-side-effects-in-reducer` — A reducer has no side effects

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the side effect has to move to a thunk, a listener or a `prepare` callback)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/no-side-effects-in-reducer.md

### What it checks

A reducer — a `createSlice` case reducer, a builder's `addCase`/`addMatcher`/`addDefaultCase`
callback, or a hand-written `(state, action)` reducer — doesn't fetch, wait, start timers, read the
clock or a random source, touch storage, or dispatch.

**Why:** A reducer must give the same next state for the same state and action, so that replaying actions
reproduces the state. *Style Guide, Priority A: Reducers Must Not Have Side Effects.*

### How to fix

1. Make random IDs and timestamps in the action's `prepare` callback, so they arrive in the payload.
2. Move fetching, timers and storage into a thunk (`createAsyncThunk`) or a listener.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'todos',
  initialState: [],
  reducers: {
    todoAdded(state, action) {
      state.push({ id: nanoid(), text: action.payload });
    },
  },
});
```

##### Do

```js
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'todos',
  initialState: [],
  reducers: {
    todoAdded: {
      reducer(state, action) {
        state.push(action.payload);
      },
      prepare(text) {
        return { payload: { id: nanoid(), text } };
      },
    },
  },
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'todos',
  initialState: [],
  reducers: {
    todoAdded(state, action) {
      state.push({ id: nanoid(), text: action.payload });
    },
  },
});
```

##### Do

```jsx
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'todos',
  initialState: [],
  reducers: {
    todoAdded: {
      reducer(state, action) {
        state.push(action.payload);
      },
      prepare(text) {
        return { payload: { id: nanoid(), text } };
      },
    },
  },
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'todos',
  initialState: [],
  reducers: {
    todoAdded(state, action) {
      state.push({ id: nanoid(), text: action.payload });
    },
  },
});
```

##### Do

```ts
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'todos',
  initialState: [],
  reducers: {
    todoAdded: {
      reducer(state, action) {
        state.push(action.payload);
      },
      prepare(text) {
        return { payload: { id: nanoid(), text } };
      },
    },
  },
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'todos',
  initialState: [],
  reducers: {
    todoAdded(state, action) {
      state.push({ id: nanoid(), text: action.payload });
    },
  },
});
```

##### Do

```tsx
const todosSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'todos',
  initialState: [],
  reducers: {
    todoAdded: {
      reducer(state, action) {
        state.push(action.payload);
      },
      prepare(text) {
        return { payload: { id: nanoid(), text } };
      },
    },
  },
});
```

## `redux-toolkit/object-shorthand-mapdispatch` — connect's mapDispatch is an object of action creators

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (each wrapped dispatch call is replaced by the action creator it calls)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/object-shorthand-mapdispatch.md

### What it checks

The second argument of `connect` from `react-redux` is an object of action creators, not a function
of `dispatch`. A function that takes `ownProps` too is left alone.

**Why:** `connect` binds an object of action creators to `dispatch` itself; the function form only repeats
that by hand. *Style Guide, Priority B: Use the Object Shorthand Form of mapDispatch with connect.*

### How to fix

1. Replace the function with an object of the action creators it wraps: `{ todoAdded }`.
2. Remove the function.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

const mapDispatch = (dispatch) => ({
  todoAdded: (text) => dispatch(todoAdded(text)),
});

export default connect(mapState, mapDispatch)(TodoList);
```

##### Do

```js
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

export default connect(mapState, { todoAdded })(TodoList);
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

const mapDispatch = (dispatch) => ({
  todoAdded: (text) => dispatch(todoAdded(text)),
});

export default connect(mapState, mapDispatch)(TodoList);
```

##### Do

```jsx
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

export default connect(mapState, { todoAdded })(TodoList);
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

const mapDispatch = (dispatch) => ({
  todoAdded: (text) => dispatch(todoAdded(text)),
});

export default connect(mapState, mapDispatch)(TodoList);
```

##### Do

```ts
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

export default connect(mapState, { todoAdded })(TodoList);
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

const mapDispatch = (dispatch) => ({
  todoAdded: (text) => dispatch(todoAdded(text)),
});

export default connect(mapState, mapDispatch)(TodoList);
```

##### Do

```tsx
import { connect } from 'react-redux';

export default connect(mapState, { todoAdded })(TodoList);
```

## `redux-toolkit/prefer-create-slice` — Reducers are written with createSlice

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the reducer, its action types and its action creators are rewritten together)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/prefer-create-slice.md

### What it checks

A Redux reducer isn't written by hand as a `switch` on `action.type` (or a chain of comparisons with
it); it is written with `createSlice`. A reducer handed to React's `useReducer` is component state,
and is left alone.

**Why:** `createSlice` writes the action types and action creators, and its reducers update an Immer draft,
so the immutable-update mistakes can't happen. *Style Guide, Priority B: Use Redux Toolkit for
Writing Redux Logic; Use Immer for Writing Immutable Updates.*

### How to fix

1. Move the initial state and each `case` into `createSlice({ name, initialState, reducers })`, one
   case reducer per action.
2. Export the generated action creators (`slice.actions`) and the reducer (`slice.reducer`), and
   replace the hand-written action types and creators with them.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
function counter(state = 0, action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'counter/incremented':
      return state + 1;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```js
const counterSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'counter',
  initialState: 0,
  reducers: {
    incremented: (state) => state + 1,
  },
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
function counter(state = 0, action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'counter/incremented':
      return state + 1;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
const counterSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'counter',
  initialState: 0,
  reducers: {
    incremented: (state) => state + 1,
  },
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
function counter(state = 0, action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'counter/incremented':
      return state + 1;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```ts
const counterSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'counter',
  initialState: 0,
  reducers: {
    incremented: (state) => state + 1,
  },
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
function counter(state = 0, action) {
  switch (action.type) {
    case 'counter/incremented':
      return state + 1;
    default:
      return state;
  }
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
const counterSlice = createSlice({
  name: 'counter',
  initialState: 0,
  reducers: {
    incremented: (state) => state + 1,
  },
});
```

## `redux-toolkit/prefer-hooks-api` — Components read the store with hooks, not connect

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the component's props and its wrapper are rewritten as hook calls)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/prefer-hooks-api.md

### What it checks

`connect` is not imported from `react-redux`; function components use `useSelector` and
`useDispatch`.

**Why:** The hooks are simpler to read and type than `connect`'s wrapper and its `mapState` and `mapDispatch`
props. *Style Guide, Priority B: Use the React-Redux Hooks API.*

### How to fix

1. In the component, call `useSelector` for each value `mapState` gave it, and `useDispatch` for the
   actions `mapDispatch` gave it.
2. Remove the `connect(…)` wrapper and export the component itself.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
import { connect } from 'react-redux';
```

##### Do

```js
import { useDispatch, useSelector } from 'react-redux';
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
import { connect } from 'react-redux';
```

##### Do

```jsx
import { useDispatch, useSelector } from 'react-redux';
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
import { connect } from 'react-redux';
```

##### Do

```ts
import { useDispatch, useSelector } from 'react-redux';
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
import { connect } from 'react-redux';
```

##### Do

```tsx
import { useDispatch, useSelector } from 'react-redux';
```

## `redux-toolkit/slice-key-names` — State slices are named after their data

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-redux-toolkit` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the key is the state's shape, so every selector that reads it changes too)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:redux-toolkit/recommended` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/redux-toolkit/slice-key-names.md

### What it checks

The keys of `combineReducers`, `combineSlices` and `configureStore`'s `reducer` object name the data
each slice holds (`users`), not the reducer that manages it (`usersReducer`).

**Why:** The key is the field every selector reads: `state.usersReducer.list` reads as code, not data.
*Style Guide, Priority B: Name State Slices Based On the Stored Data.*

### How to fix

1. Rename the key after the data: `users: usersReducer`.
2. Update every selector and test that reads the old key.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const rootReducer = combineReducers({ usersReducer, postsReducer });
```

##### Do

```js
const rootReducer = combineReducers({ users: usersReducer, posts: postsReducer });
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const rootReducer = combineReducers({ usersReducer, postsReducer });
```

##### Do

```jsx
const rootReducer = combineReducers({ users: usersReducer, posts: postsReducer });
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const rootReducer = combineReducers({ usersReducer, postsReducer });
```

##### Do

```ts
const rootReducer = combineReducers({ users: usersReducer, posts: postsReducer });
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const rootReducer = combineReducers({ usersReducer, postsReducer });
```

##### Do

```tsx
const rootReducer = combineReducers({ users: usersReducer, posts: postsReducer });
```

## `scss/at-extend-no-missing-placeholder` — `@extend` targets a placeholder

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (turning a class into a placeholder changes the stylesheet's output)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/at-extend-no-missing-placeholder.md

### What it checks

`@extend` names a `%placeholder`, not a class or an element.

**Why:** Extending a class drags every selector that mentions the class into the output, including ones far from the code at hand.

### How to fix

1. Move the shared declarations into a `%placeholder`.
2. `@extend` the placeholder from each place that needs it.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  @extend .b;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
%b {
  color: red;
}

.a {
  @extend %b;
}
```

### Differences from the source

A target with interpolation is not judged.

## `scss/at-if-no-null` — No comparing to `null` in `@if`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/at-if-no-null.md

### What it checks

`@if` tests a value directly: `@if $x`, `@if not $x`, not `@if $x != null` or `@if $x == null`.

**Why:** Every value other than `null` and `false` is truthy in Sass, so testing the value says the same thing in fewer words.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@if $x != null {
  a: b;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@if $x {
  a: b;
}
```

### Differences from the source

`$x != null` is fixed to `$x` and `$x == null` to `not $x`. A comparison that is only part of a condition is reported without a fix.

## `scss/at-mixin-pattern` — Mixin names are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every `@include` of the mixin)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/at-mixin-pattern.md

### What it checks

Mixin names match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression a mixin name must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the mixin to match the pattern.
2. Rename every `@include` of it.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@mixin ButtonBase {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@mixin button-base {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Only the definition is checked.

## `scss/at-rule-no-unknown` — No unknown at-rules (SCSS)

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended at-rule is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/at-rule-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Every at-rule is one CSS or Sass defines: `@mixin`, `@include`, `@use`, `@if`, `@each` and the rest of Sass's own are known. This rule replaces `css/at-rule-no-unknown` on `.scss` files, which does not know Sass.

**Why:** A browser skips a CSS at-rule it does not know, block and all, and Sass passes an unknown one through, so a typo silently disables its contents.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreAtRules` | `string[]` | `[]` | at-rules to accept, such as a framework's; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### How to fix

1. Correct the at-rule name.
2. If a build tool handles it, add it to `ignoreAtRules`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@mixn button {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@mixin button {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Sass's at-rules are always known; the rule checks the CSS at-rules against the same table as `css/at-rule-no-unknown`.

## `scss/dollar-variable-pattern` — `$variables` are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every use of the variable)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/dollar-variable-pattern.md

### What it checks

`$variable` names match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression the name, without its `$`, must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the variable to match the pattern.
2. Rename every use of it.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
$FontSize: 16px;
```

##### Do

```scss
$font-size: 16px;
```

### Differences from the source

The pattern applies to declarations, not to the names in an `@each` or a mixin's parameter list.

## `scss/double-slash-comment-empty` — No empty `//` comments

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/double-slash-comment-empty.md

### What it checks

A `//` comment holds something. An empty one is removed.

**Why:** An empty comment says nothing; it is usually left over from an edit.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  //
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.a {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

A `///` SassDoc line is not empty.

## `scss/function-no-unknown` — No unknown functions (SCSS)

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (the intended function is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/function-no-unknown.md

### What it checks

Every function called is a CSS function, a Sass built-in (global or `module.name`), or one the file defines with `@function`. A file that loads names it cannot see — `@import`, or `@use … as *` — is not checked.

**Why:** A browser drops a declaration whose value has an unknown function, and Sass passes the call through as plain CSS, so a typo fails silently.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ignoreFunctions` | `string[]` | `[]` | functions to accept; `/regex/` for a pattern |

### How to fix

1. Correct the function name.
2. If it comes from a library, call it through its module (`lib.name()`), or add it to `ignoreFunctions`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  width: percentag(0.5);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "sass:math";

.a {
  width: math.percentage(0.5);
}
```

### Differences from the source

Calls through a namespace (`ns.name()`) are not judged: the namespace's members are outside the file.

## `scss/load-no-partial-leading-underscore` — No leading underscore in a loaded partial

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/load-no-partial-leading-underscore.md

### What it checks

`@use`, `@forward` and `@import` name a partial without its leading underscore: `@use "colors"`, not `@use "_colors"`.

**Why:** Sass finds `_colors.scss` from `"colors"`; the underscore in the path is noise, and a file renamed to drop it breaks every load.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@use "base/_colors";
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "base/colors";
```

### Differences from the source

Plain CSS imports (`.css`, URLs) and `sass:` modules are skipped.

## `scss/max-nesting-depth` — Limit nesting depth

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (flattening a selector is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/max-nesting-depth.md

### What it checks

A style rule nests at most `max` levels inside other style rules (default 3): `.a { .b { .c { .d {} } } }` is three levels of nesting.

**Why:** Deep nesting couples a rule to the markup's shape, raises specificity, and produces long selectors nobody wrote on purpose.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max` | `number` | `3` | the deepest nesting allowed |

### How to fix

1. Lift the inner rule out and give it its own class.
2. Use `&-suffix` (BEM-style names) instead of a new level.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  .b {
    .c {
      .d {
        .e {
          color: red;
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

##### Do

```scss
.a {
  .b {
    .c {
      .d {
        color: red;
      }
    }
  }
}
```

### Differences from the source

Nested properties (`font: { … }`) and at-rules such as `@media` and `@include` do not count as a level; only style rules do.

## `scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables` — No duplicate `$variables`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (which declaration wins is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-duplicate-dollar-variables.md

### What it checks

A `$variable` is declared once per scope. A later `!default` declaration is not a duplicate, and a variable declared in another block is a different one.

**Why:** The second declaration silently replaces the first, so the first is dead code or a mistake.

### How to fix

1. Delete the declaration that should not win.
2. Rename one of them if both are meant.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
$gap: 4px;
$gap: 8px;
```

##### Do

```scss
$gap: 4px;
$gap-large: 8px;
```

### Differences from the source

`ignoreDefaults` is always on: a `!default` redeclaration is accepted.

## `scss/no-duplicate-mixins` — No duplicate mixins

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (which definition should stay is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-duplicate-mixins.md

### What it checks

A mixin is defined once per scope.

**Why:** The later definition replaces the earlier one; every `@include` before it silently gets the other body.

### How to fix

1. Delete or rename one of the definitions.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@mixin shadow {
  box-shadow: none;
}
@mixin shadow {
  box-shadow: 0 0 1px;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@mixin shadow {
  box-shadow: none;
}
@mixin shadow-soft {
  box-shadow: 0 0 1px;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Two scopes may use the same name.

## `scss/no-global-function-names` — No global function names

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-global-function-names.md

### What it checks

The built-in functions Dart Sass moved into modules are called through their module: `map.get()`, not `map-get()`; `math.percentage()`, not `percentage()`. Functions that are also plain CSS (`min`, `max`, `round`, `abs`, `grayscale`, `invert`, `saturate`, `opacity`) are not reported: a call to one may be CSS.

**Why:** The global names are deprecated in Dart Sass and go away in 3.0. Module functions also keep a file's names from colliding.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  width: map-get($sizes, small);
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "sass:map";

.a {
  width: map.get($sizes, small);
}
```

### Differences from the source

stylelint-scss reports the global names it lists; this rule reports the module-moved built-ins and fixes the renames, adding each `@use "sass:…"` once. The colour adjusters are reported without a fix.

## `scss/no-import` — No `@import`

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`@use` namespaces what it loads and loads it once, so a bare swap can change what resolves)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-import.md

### What it checks

`@import` is not used for Sass files: Dart Sass deprecates it and removes it in 3.0. Load a file with `@use`, or re-export it with `@forward`. An import that stays a plain CSS `@import` (a `url()`, an `http://` address, a `.css` file, or one with a media query) is allowed.

**Why:** `@import` puts everything it loads in one global scope; two files can silently overwrite each other's variables and mixins, and a file imported twice is compiled twice.

### How to fix

1. Replace `@import "file"` with `@use "file"`; the members are then reached as `file.$name`, `file.mixin()`.
2. Use `@use "file" as *` to keep the old unprefixed names while migrating.
3. In an index file that only gathers other files, use `@forward`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
@import "variables";
@import "mixins";
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "variables";
@use "mixins";
```

### Differences from the source

Plain CSS imports are not reported. The fix is offered for a single quoted path; it is `suggest` because `@use` changes how the file's members are named.

## `scss/no-slash-division` — No `/` as division

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`math.div` needs a `@use` of sass:math, and a slash may be CSS)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/no-slash-division.md

### What it checks

Division is written `math.div($a, $b)`, not `$a / $b`. A `/` that Sass treats as a plain separator is left alone: `font: 12px/1.5`, `grid-area: 1 / 2`, and anything inside `calc()`.

**Why:** Dart Sass deprecates `/` as division and removes it in 3.0; the slash is ambiguous with CSS separators.

### How to fix

1. Add `@use "sass:math";` at the top of the file.
2. Replace `$a / $b` with `math.div($a, $b)`.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
.a {
  width: $total / 3;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
@use "sass:math";

.a {
  width: math.div($total, 3);
}
```

### Differences from the source

The check is by operand: a `$variable`, or numbers inside a parenthesised expression. `font: 12px/1.5` is never reported.

## `scss/percent-placeholder-pattern` — `%placeholder` names are kebab-case

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-scss` · `codelaw-rules-scss` · **Languages:** SCSS
- **Fix:** `manual` (renaming must update every `@extend` of the placeholder)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:scss/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/scss/percent-placeholder-pattern.md

### What it checks

Placeholder selector names match a pattern, kebab-case by default.

**Why:** A consistent scheme makes names predictable across a codebase.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pattern` | `string` | `"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"` | a regular expression a placeholder name, without its `%`, must match |

### How to fix

1. Rename the placeholder to match the pattern.
2. Rename every `@extend` of it.

### Examples

#### SCSS

##### Don't

```scss
%ButtonBase {
  color: red;
}
```

##### Do

```scss
%button-base {
  color: red;
}
```

### Differences from the source

Only definitions are checked.

## `sec-html/angularjs-url-expression` — AngularJS URLs use ng-href and ng-src

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the expression's value should be checked too; the rename is only the first step)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/angularjs-url-expression.md

### What it checks

In a page that uses AngularJS, `href="{{…}}"` and `src="{{…}}"` are written `ng-href` and `ng-src`.

**Why:** The browser requests the literal `{{…}}` before AngularJS fills it in, and an unvetted expression in a URL is an injection point; the `ng-` forms are set only after interpolation.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div ng-app><a href="{{ profileUrl }}">Profile</a></div>
```

##### Do

```html
<div ng-app><a ng-href="{{ profileUrl }}">Profile</a></div>
```

## `sec-html/csp-meta-unsafe` — A meta Content Security Policy does not allow unsafe script

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the page's scripts have to be given nonces or hashes, or moved to files)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/csp-meta-unsafe.md

### What it checks

A `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy">` does not allow `'unsafe-inline'`, `'unsafe-eval'`, `*` or `data:` as a script source.

**Why:** Each of them lets injected script run, which is what the policy exists to stop.

### How to fix

1. Move inline script into files, or give it a nonce or a hash (`'nonce-…'`, `'sha256-…'`).
2. Remove `'unsafe-eval'` and replace `eval`, `new Function` and string timers.
3. List the origins scripts load from instead of `*` or `data:`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'">
```

##### Do

```html
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="script-src 'self' 'nonce-r4nd0m'">
```

## `sec-html/form-csrf-token` — A POST form carries a CSRF token

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (which token the server checks depends on its framework)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/form-csrf-token.md

### What it checks

A `<form method="post">` has a hidden anti-forgery field, or a template tag that writes one.

**Why:** Without a token another site can submit the form with the signed-in user's cookies.

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `names` | `string[]` | `[]` | extra names (field names or template tags) that count as a CSRF token, besides csrf, xsrf, authenticity_token, antiforgery, csrfmiddlewaretoken, __requestverificationtoken and _token |

### How to fix

1. Add the framework's field: `{% csrf_token %}` (Django), `@csrf` (Laravel), `<%= csrf_meta_tags %>` / `authenticity_token` (Rails), `{{ form.hidden_tag() }}` (Flask-WTF), or a hidden `_csrf` input.
2. If the form posts to another site, ignore it with `exceptions`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<form method="post" action="/transfer"><input name="to"></form>
```

##### Do

```html
<form method="post" action="/transfer"><input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}"><input name="to"></form>
```

## `sec-html/iframe-allow-powerful` — A cross-origin iframe is not given a powerful feature

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (which framed sites deserve the permission is the owner's decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/iframe-allow-powerful.md

### What it checks

An `<iframe>` whose `src` is on another origin does not list `camera`, `microphone`, `geolocation`, `payment` or another powerful feature in `allow`.

**Why:** The framed site gets the permission prompt, with the page's name on it, and whatever that site serves later inherits the grant.

### How to fix

1. Drop the feature from `allow`.
2. Or limit it to the origin that needs it: `allow="camera https://meet.example.com"`, and keep `'none'` for the rest.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<iframe src="https://meet.example.com/room" allow="camera; microphone"></iframe>
```

##### Do

```html
<iframe src="https://meet.example.com/room" allow="fullscreen"></iframe>
```

## `sec-html/iframe-sandbox` — An iframe is sandboxed

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the framed page may need `allow-*` tokens, which only its author knows)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/iframe-sandbox.md

### What it checks

An `<iframe>` has a `sandbox` attribute, and one that allows scripts does not also allow the same origin.

**Why:** A framed page without `sandbox` runs with every power a top-level page has; `allow-scripts` with `allow-same-origin` lets it remove its own sandbox.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<iframe src="/widget"></iframe>
```

##### Do

```html
<iframe sandbox src="/widget"></iframe>
```

## `sec-html/no-credentials-in-url` — No username and password in a URL

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the credential should live is the author's decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-credentials-in-url.md

### What it checks

A URL attribute does not carry `user:password@` in front of its host.

**Why:** A URL is stored in history, logs, referrers and bookmarks, so a credential written into one is disclosed to all of them.

### How to fix

1. Remove the credentials from the URL.
2. Send them in an `Authorization` header, or keep the request on the server.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<a href="https://admin:hunter2@intranet.example.com/">Admin</a>
```

##### Do

```html
<a href="https://intranet.example.com/">Admin</a>
```

## `sec-html/no-external-base` — <base> stays on this origin

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (which origin the page may use is a decision for its owner)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-external-base.md

### What it checks

A `<base href>` is a path, not a URL on another origin.

**Why:** Every relative URL, form action and script on the page resolves against `<base>`, so one that points elsewhere hands them all to that site.

### How to fix

1. Delete the `<base>` and write the URLs you need in full.
2. Or make its `href` a path on this origin, such as `/app/`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<base href="https://cdn.example.com/app/">
```

##### Do

```html
<base href="/app/">
```

## `sec-html/no-inline-event-handler` — No inline event handlers

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the handler's code has to move into a script that attaches it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-inline-event-handler.md

### What it checks

No element has an inline event handler (`onclick`, `onerror`, `onload`, …).

**Why:** An inline handler runs script from an attribute, so a strict Content Security Policy that blocks inline script blocks it too, and a value interpolated into it becomes cross-site scripting.

### How to fix

1. Give the element an id or a class.
2. Attach the listener with `addEventListener` in a script file.
3. Delete the `on…` attribute.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<button type="button" onclick="save()">Save</button>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button" id="save">Save</button>
```

## `sec-html/no-javascript-url` — No javascript: URLs

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the script has to move out of the URL into a listener or a real link)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-javascript-url.md

### What it checks

An `href`, `src`, `action`, `formaction`, `xlink:href` or `<object data>` is never a `javascript:` URL.

**Why:** A `javascript:` URL runs script from an attribute, so it is cross-site scripting waiting for one interpolated value, and a strict Content Security Policy blocks it.

### How to fix

1. Replace a `javascript:` link with a `<button type="button">` and attach the listener with `addEventListener`.
2. Point `href`, `src`, `action` or `formaction` at a real URL.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<a href="javascript:void(0)">Menu</a>
```

##### Do

```html
<button type="button" id="menu">Menu</button>
```

## `sec-html/no-mixed-content` — Subresources and forms load over HTTPS

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the host may not serve HTTPS; check that it does before switching)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-mixed-content.md

### What it checks

A `src`, a form `action`, a stylesheet or script `href` and a download link never use `http://`.

**Why:** A resource fetched over plain HTTP can be read and changed by anyone on the network, and a browser blocks or warns about it on an HTTPS page.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<script src="http://cdn.example.com/lib.js"></script>
```

##### Do

```html
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js"></script>
```

## `sec-html/no-plugin-embed` — No <object>, <embed> or <applet>

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (what replaces the plugin depends on what it showed)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-plugin-embed.md

### What it checks

The page does not use `<object>`, `<embed>` or `<applet>` (an `<object>` that holds an image is fine).

**Why:** They load a plugin or another document with the page's trust, and the plugins that needed them are gone from browsers.

### How to fix

1. Use `<img>`, `<video>` or `<audio>` for media.
2. Use a sandboxed `<iframe>` for another document.
3. Use `<a download>` for a file to fetch.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<embed src="movie.swf">
```

##### Do

```html
<video src="movie.mp4" controls></video>
```

## `sec-html/no-secret-in-hidden-input` — No secret in a hidden input

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the secret should live is a design decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-secret-in-hidden-input.md

### What it checks

A hidden input named like a password, token, secret or API key does not hold a literal value (CSRF tokens are excluded).

**Why:** A hidden field is part of the page everyone receives, so a secret written into it is disclosed to every visitor.

### How to fix

1. Keep the secret on the server and send a session or a reference instead.
2. If the field is an anti-forgery token, name it `csrf_token`, `_csrf` or the framework's own name.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<input type="hidden" name="api_key" value="sk_live_51Habc">
```

##### Do

```html
<input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}">
```

## `sec-html/no-sensitive-comments` — No comment that exposes a secret or an internal host

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `auto`
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-sensitive-comments.md

### What it checks

An HTML comment does not hold a password, key, token, private IP address, internal host name, or a note to remove it before release.

**Why:** Comments are sent to every visitor, so a developer's note becomes a disclosure.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<!-- password: hunter2 -->
<p>Welcome</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<p>Welcome</p>
```

## `sec-html/no-srcdoc-script` — An iframe's srcdoc holds no script

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (the framed document has to become a file or be sandboxed)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-srcdoc-script.md

### What it checks

An `<iframe srcdoc>` does not contain a `<script>`, an event handler or a `javascript:` URL.

**Why:** `srcdoc` content runs with the origin of the page that holds it unless the iframe is sandboxed, so script in it is script in the page.

### How to fix

1. Move the document to its own file and load it with `src`.
2. Add `sandbox` without `allow-same-origin`.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<iframe srcdoc="&lt;script&gt;track()&lt;/script&gt;"></iframe>
```

##### Do

```html
<iframe sandbox src="/track.html"></iframe>
```

## `sec-html/no-template-html-sink` — No template binding that writes HTML

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the value is trusted, and how to sanitise it, is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-template-html-sink.md

### What it checks

A template does not bind a value as HTML: Angular `[innerHTML]` and `[outerHTML]`, Vue `v-html`, Alpine `x-html`.

**Why:** The value is written into the page as markup, so any part of it a user controls is cross-site scripting.

### How to fix

1. Bind text instead (`{{ value }}`, `v-text`, `x-text`, `[textContent]`).
2. If it must be HTML, sanitise it with a maintained library such as DOMPurify and bind the sanitised result.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<div [innerHTML]="comment"></div>
```

##### Do

```html
<div>{{ comment }}</div>
```

## `sec-html/no-unsafe-template-interpolation` — No template syntax that turns escaping off

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether the value is trusted, and how to sanitise it, is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/no-unsafe-template-interpolation.md

### What it checks

A template does not turn escaping off: Handlebars `{{{ }}}`, Jinja and Nunjucks `|safe`, Django `{% autoescape off %}`, EJS `<%-`.

**Why:** The value is written into the page as markup, so any part of it a user controls is cross-site scripting.

### How to fix

1. Use the escaping form: `{{ value }}` (Handlebars, Jinja, Django), `<%= value %>` (EJS).
2. If the value must be markup, sanitise it with a maintained library first and mark only the sanitised result safe.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<p>{{{ comment }}}</p>
```

##### Do

```html
<p>{{ comment }}</p>
```

## `sec-html/password-form-post` — A form with a password sends it with POST over HTTPS

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a server that reads only the query string has to change with the form)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/password-form-post.md

### What it checks

A form holding a password field sets `method="post"` and does not post to an `http:` URL.

**Why:** A form with no `method` or with `method="get"` puts the password in the URL, where history, logs and referrers keep it; an `http:` action sends it in the clear.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<form action="/login" method="get"><input type="password" name="pw"></form>
```

##### Do

```html
<form action="/login" method="post"><input type="password" name="pw"></form>
```

## `sec-html/referrer-policy` — No referrer policy that leaks full URLs

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a partner may rely on the full referrer; the safer value is a suggestion)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/referrer-policy.md

### What it checks

A `referrerpolicy` attribute or `<meta name="referrer">` is not `unsafe-url` or `no-referrer-when-downgrade`.

**Why:** Both send the full URL of the page, query string included, to other sites, and a URL often holds a token or an identifier.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<a href="https://other.example/" referrerpolicy="unsafe-url">Other</a>
```

##### Do

```html
<a href="https://other.example/" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin">Other</a>
```

## `sec-html/sri-crossorigin` — A script or stylesheet with an integrity hash has crossorigin

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-html` · `codelaw-rules-security-html` · **Languages:** HTML
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`anonymous` is right unless the file needs credentials; the suggestion assumes it does not)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-html/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-html/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-html/sri-crossorigin.md

### What it checks

A `<script>` or `<link>` from another origin that has `integrity` also has `crossorigin`.

**Why:** Without `crossorigin` the browser fetches the file without CORS and cannot read it to check the hash, so the `integrity` protects nothing.

### Examples

#### HTML

##### Don't

```html
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js" integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC"></script>
```

##### Do

```html
<script src="https://cdn.example.com/lib.js" integrity="sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
```

## `sec-js/angularjs-sce-disabled` — No AngularJS strict contextual escaping switched off

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (which sources the application loads from is a decision for the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `warn` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/angularjs-sce-disabled.md

### What it checks

AngularJS's `$sce` stays on, `resourceUrlWhitelist` has no `"**"`, the href and image whitelists are not match-everything, and `$sce.trustAs*` is not given an unsanitized value.

**Your sanitizer:** a value passes when it is a call to one of the `sanitizers`: the built-in list (DOMPurify, sanitize-html, xss, escape-html, lodash and he `escape`, Trusted Types `createHTML`) plus your own, each matched by name and by the module it is imported from, so a local `function sanitize(x) { return x }` does not pass. `sanitizers_mode = "replace"` makes yours the only ones that count. It does not follow a value through a variable: `const c = clean(x)` then `c` at the sink is not a call. Add a project function with `sanitizers = [{ name = "sanitizeHtml", module = "@acme/security" }]`.

**Why:** `$sce` is what stops a bound string from becoming HTML, a script or a frame source; switching it off or trusting every value turns each binding into an XSS sink (CWE-79).

### Options

| Option | Type | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sanitizers` | `call[]` | 10 entries (below) | functions whose result may reach the sink: a callee path (global) or { name, module }; `sanitizers_mode: replace` makes them the only ones that count |
| `sanitizers_mode` | `string` | `"extend"` | `extend` adds your `sanitizers` to the default list; `replace` uses only yours |

### How to fix

1. Leave `$sceProvider.enabled` at its default (`true`).
2. List the hosts a template may load from in `resourceUrlWhitelist`: `["self", "https://cdn.example.com/**"]`, not `"**"`.
3. Pass a value to `$sce.trustAsHtml` only after a sanitizer (`$sanitize`, DOMPurify) has cleaned it.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(false);
});
```

##### Do

```js
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(true);
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(false);
});
```

##### Do

```jsx
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(true);
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(false);
});
```

##### Do

```ts
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
  $sceProvider.enabled(true);
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
app.config(function ($sceProvider) {
```
