##### Do

```tsx
const hash = crypto.pbkdf2Sync(password, salt, 600000, 32, "sha256");
```

## `sec-js/postmessage-origin` — postMessage names its target, a message handler checks the sender

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (the origin to name is known only to the application)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/postmessage-origin.md

### What it checks

`postMessage` is given a target origin, not `"*"`, and a `message` listener that is a function reads `event.origin` before it trusts `event.data`.

**Why:** With `"*"` any page that holds the window receives the message, and a listener that skips the origin check accepts messages from any page that can open or frame this one (CWE-346).

### How to fix

1. Give `postMessage` the exact origin of the receiver as its second argument.
2. In the listener, compare `event.origin` with the exact origin you expect (not `includes` or `endsWith`) and return before touching `event.data`.
3. Check `event.source` is the window you opened or framed when more than one window can send.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
parent.postMessage(payload, "*");
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  use(event.data);
});
```

##### Do

```js
parent.postMessage(payload, "https://app.example.com");
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  if (event.origin !== "https://app.example.com") return;
  use(event.data);
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
parent.postMessage(payload, "*");
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  use(event.data);
});
```

##### Do

```jsx
parent.postMessage(payload, "https://app.example.com");
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  if (event.origin !== "https://app.example.com") return;
  use(event.data);
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
parent.postMessage(payload, "*");
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  use(event.data);
});
```

##### Do

```ts
parent.postMessage(payload, "https://app.example.com");
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  if (event.origin !== "https://app.example.com") return;
  use(event.data);
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
parent.postMessage(payload, "*");
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  use(event.data);
});
```

##### Do

```tsx
parent.postMessage(payload, "https://app.example.com");
window.addEventListener("message", (event) => {
  if (event.origin !== "https://app.example.com") return;
  use(event.data);
});
```

## `sec-js/timing-safe-compare` — A token, hash or signature is compared in constant time

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`timingSafeEqual` throws when the two buffers differ in length, so the length has to be compared first)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `warn` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/timing-safe-compare.md

### What it checks

A value named like a token, an HMAC, a signature, a digest, a secret or a CSRF token is not compared with `===` or `==`: `crypto.timingSafeEqual` does it.

**Why:** `===` stops at the first byte that differs, so the time it takes tells an attacker how many leading bytes they got right, and they can guess a secret byte by byte (CWE-208).

### How to fix

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
if (providedToken === expectedToken) {
  grant();
}
```

##### Do

```js
if (crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(providedToken), Buffer.from(expectedToken))) {
  grant();
}
```

##### Fixed

```js
if (crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(providedToken), Buffer.from(expectedToken))) {
  grant();
}
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
if (providedToken === expectedToken) {
  grant();
}
```

##### Do

```jsx
if (crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(providedToken), Buffer.from(expectedToken))) {
  grant();
}
```

##### Fixed

```jsx
if (crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(providedToken), Buffer.from(expectedToken))) {
  grant();
}
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
if (providedToken === expectedToken) {
  grant();
}
```

##### Do

```ts
if (crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(providedToken), Buffer.from(expectedToken))) {
  grant();
}
```

##### Fixed

```ts
if (crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(providedToken), Buffer.from(expectedToken))) {
  grant();
}
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
if (providedToken === expectedToken) {
  grant();
}
```

##### Do

```tsx
if (crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(providedToken), Buffer.from(expectedToken))) {
  grant();
}
```

##### Fixed

```tsx
if (crypto.timingSafeEqual(Buffer.from(providedToken), Buffer.from(expectedToken))) {
  grant();
}
```

## `sec-js/upload-limits` — multer has size limits and a file filter

- **Pack:** `@codelaw/rules-security-js` · `codelaw-rules-security-js` · **Languages:** JavaScript, JSX, TypeScript, TSX
- **Fix:** `manual` (which sizes and types are allowed is a decision for the author)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-js/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-js/strict` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-ts/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-js/upload-limits.md

### What it checks

`multer(…)` is given both `limits` and `fileFilter`.

**Why:** Without a size limit one request fills the disk or memory, and without a filter any file type is stored and may later be served as a page or run (CWE-434, CWE-770).

### How to fix

1. Set `limits: { fileSize, files }` to what the feature needs.
2. Write a `fileFilter` that accepts only the types the feature handles, and check the file's content, not its name or `mimetype` alone.
3. Store uploads outside the web root, under a name the server picks.

### Examples

#### JavaScript

##### Don't

```js
const upload = multer({ dest: "uploads/" });
```

##### Do

```js
const upload = multer({
  dest: "uploads/",
  limits: { fileSize: 1000000, files: 1 },
  fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => cb(null, file.mimetype === "image/png"),
});
```

#### JSX

##### Don't

```jsx
const upload = multer({ dest: "uploads/" });
```

##### Do

```jsx
const upload = multer({
  dest: "uploads/",
  limits: { fileSize: 1000000, files: 1 },
  fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => cb(null, file.mimetype === "image/png"),
});
```

#### TypeScript

##### Don't

```ts
const upload = multer({ dest: "uploads/" });
```

##### Do

```ts
const upload = multer({
  dest: "uploads/",
  limits: { fileSize: 1000000, files: 1 },
  fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => cb(null, file.mimetype === "image/png"),
});
```

#### TSX

##### Don't

```tsx
const upload = multer({ dest: "uploads/" });
```

##### Do

```tsx
const upload = multer({
  dest: "uploads/",
  limits: { fileSize: 1000000, files: 1 },
  fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => cb(null, file.mimetype === "image/png"),
});
```

## `sec-py/cookie-flags` — Cookies are `Secure`, `HttpOnly` and `SameSite`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`secure=True` stops the cookie being set over plain HTTP in development, and `HttpOnly` hides it from scripts that read it on purpose)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/cookie-flags.md

### What it checks

`set_cookie` passes `secure`, `httponly` and `samesite`, and none of them is `False` or `None`.

**Why:** Without `Secure` the cookie travels over plain HTTP, without `HttpOnly` a script can read it, and without `SameSite` other sites can send it along (CWE-614, CWE-1004).

### How to fix

1. Add `secure=True, httponly=True, samesite="Lax"`.
2. Use `samesite="Strict"` for a session cookie; `None` needs `secure=True` and a reason.
3. A cookie a script must read can omit `httponly`; say so in a comment.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
resp.set_cookie("sid", sid)
```

##### Do

```py
resp.set_cookie("sid", sid, secure=True, httponly=True, samesite="Lax")
```

##### Fixed

```py
resp.set_cookie("sid", sid, secure=True, httponly=True, samesite="Lax")
```

## `sec-py/django-settings` — Django settings are safe

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the production value comes from the deployment (environment variables, a secret manager))
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/django-settings.md

### What it checks

In a settings module, `DEBUG`, `ALLOWED_HOSTS`, `SECRET_KEY` and the cookie flags are not left in their development values.

**Why:** Debug pages show settings and source (CWE-489); `ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["*"]` accepts forged Host headers; a literal `SECRET_KEY` is in the repository (CWE-798); cookies without `Secure` travel over plain HTTP (CWE-614).

### How to fix

1. `DEBUG = os.environ.get("DJANGO_DEBUG") == "1"`.
2. `ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["app.example.com"]`: list the host names you serve.
3. `SECRET_KEY = os.environ["DJANGO_SECRET_KEY"]`, and rotate the one that was committed.
4. Set `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`, `CSRF_COOKIE_SECURE` and `SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT` to `True`; run `python manage.py check --deploy`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py path=settings.py
DEBUG = True
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["*"]
```

##### Do

```py path=settings.py
import os

DEBUG = os.environ.get("DJANGO_DEBUG") == "1"
ALLOWED_HOSTS = ["app.example.com"]
```

## `sec-py/fastapi-cors` — CORS does not allow every origin with credentials

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the list of trusted origins is the application's own)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/fastapi-cors.md

### What it checks

`CORSMiddleware` is not given `allow_origins=["*"]` together with `allow_credentials=True`.

**Why:** Any site can then make authenticated requests as the user and read the answers (CWE-942).

### How to fix

1. List the origins: `allow_origins=["https://app.example.com"]`.
2. If the API needs no cookies, set `allow_credentials=False` and keep `*`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["*"], allow_credentials=True)
```

##### Do

```py
app.add_middleware(CORSMiddleware, allow_origins=["https://app.example.com"], allow_credentials=True)
```

## `sec-py/flask-debug` — Flask's debugger is off

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the setting belongs to the environment, so the debug flag has to come from configuration)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/flask-debug.md

### What it checks

`app.run(debug=True)` is not written in code.

**Why:** The debugger serves an interactive console that runs code on the server, and a stack trace shows source and settings (CWE-489).

### How to fix

1. Remove `debug=True`; turn the debugger on with `flask --debug run` while developing.
2. In production run a WSGI server (`gunicorn app:app`), not `app.run`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)
app.run(debug=True)
```

##### Do

```py
from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)
app.run()
```

## `sec-py/flask-settings` — Flask configuration is safe

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the production values come from the deployment (environment variables, a secret manager))
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/flask-settings.md

### What it checks

`SECRET_KEY` is not a literal, and `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED` and `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE` are not switched off in the app configuration.

**Why:** A literal key is in the repository (CWE-798), turning off CSRF protection lets other sites submit forms as the user (CWE-352), and a cookie without `Secure` travels over plain HTTP (CWE-614).

### How to fix

1. `app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = os.environ["FLASK_SECRET_KEY"]`, and rotate the key that was committed.
2. Leave `WTF_CSRF_ENABLED` on; send the token with `{{ csrf_token() }}`.
3. Set `SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE`, `SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY` and `SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE` to safe values.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = "dev-secret-key"
```

##### Do

```py
import os

app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = os.environ["FLASK_SECRET_KEY"]
```

## `sec-py/hf-pin-revision` — Hugging Face downloads pin a revision

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the commit hash to pin is a choice the author makes after reviewing the model)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/hf-pin-revision.md

### What it checks

`from_pretrained`, `hf_hub_download`, `snapshot_download` and `load_dataset` are called with `revision=`.

**Why:** Without a revision the code runs whatever the repository's `main` branch holds today, so a change there reaches production unreviewed (CWE-494).

### How to fix

1. Find the commit hash of the revision you reviewed on the model's page.
2. Pass it: `from_pretrained(name, revision="<hash>")`.
3. Keep the hash in one constant or setting so an upgrade is one reviewed change.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from transformers import AutoModel

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("org/model")
```

##### Do

```py
from transformers import AutoModel

MODEL_REVISION = "5c9e4d1"
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("org/model", revision=MODEL_REVISION)
```

## `sec-py/jinja-autoescape` — Jinja2 keeps autoescape on

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (turning autoescape on changes the output of templates that write HTML on purpose; those need `|safe` or `Markup`)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/jinja-autoescape.md

### What it checks

`Environment` is not created with `autoescape=False` or without `autoescape`, and `render_template_string` / `Template` / `from_string` are not given a template that is not a literal.

**Why:** Without autoescape a value written into a page can carry a script (CWE-79); a template built from a non-literal runs template code on the server (CWE-1336).

### How to fix

1. Create the environment with `autoescape=True`, or `select_autoescape()`.
2. Never use request data as the template: pass it as a value to a template file instead.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from jinja2 import Environment

env = Environment(autoescape=False)
```

##### Do

```py
from jinja2 import Environment

env = Environment(autoescape=True)
```

##### Fixed

```py
from jinja2 import Environment

env = Environment(autoescape=True)
```

## `sec-py/logging-listen` — `logging.config.listen` is not used

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (reconfiguring a running process needs another route (a signal handler, a config reload) the author has to choose)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/logging-listen.md

### What it checks

`logging.config.listen()` is not called.

**Why:** It opens a socket that accepts a logging configuration, which can name any callable to run, so anyone who can connect runs code (CWE-94).

### How to fix

1. Remove the call; load the configuration from a file at start-up with `logging.config.dictConfig`.
2. To change levels at run time use a signal handler that re-reads the file.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import logging.config

t = logging.config.listen(9999)
```

##### Do

```py
import logging.config

logging.config.dictConfig(CONFIG)
```

## `sec-py/ml-unsafe-load` — Model and array files are not unpickled

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the replacement format (`safetensors`, `.npy` without pickle, Parquet) means converting the stored files)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/ml-unsafe-load.md

### What it checks

`numpy.load(allow_pickle=True)`, `joblib.load`, `pandas.read_pickle` and Keras `load_model(safe_mode=False)` are not used.

**Why:** Each one unpickles the file, so a model or dataset from anywhere else runs code on load (CWE-502).

### How to fix

1. Save and load arrays with `np.save` / `np.load` without `allow_pickle`, and tensors with `safetensors`.
2. Store tables as Parquet or CSV, not pickle.
3. If the file must be a pickle, load only files your own pipeline wrote and check a signature first.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import numpy as np

arr = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True)
```

##### Do

```py
import numpy as np

arr = np.load(path)
```

## `sec-py/no-assert-for-auth` — `assert` is not an access check

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the replacement raises the right exception for the framework, which only the author knows)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-assert-for-auth.md

### What it checks

A permission, role or authentication test is not written as an `assert`.

**Why:** `python -O` removes every `assert`, so the check disappears in an optimised run (CWE-703).

### How to fix

1. Replace it with `if not user.is_authenticated: raise PermissionDenied`.
2. Use your framework's decorator (`@login_required`, `Depends(...)`) where one fits.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def delete(request, item):
    assert request.user.is_staff
```

##### Do

```py
from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied

def delete(request, item):
    if not request.user.is_staff:
        raise PermissionDenied
```

## `sec-py/no-bind-all-interfaces` — A server does not bind to every interface in code

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the address belongs in configuration, with a loopback default)
- **Severity when named:** `warn` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-bind-all-interfaces.md

### What it checks

A socket or server is not bound to `0.0.0.0` in the source.

**Why:** The service is then reachable from every network the machine is on, including ones that were not meant to reach it (CWE-605).

### How to fix

1. Bind to `127.0.0.1` by default and take the address from an environment variable.
2. A container that must listen on every interface sets it in its deployment settings, not in the code.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import uvicorn

uvicorn.run(app, host="0.0.0.0")
```

##### Do

```py
import os
import uvicorn

uvicorn.run(app, host=os.environ.get("HOST", "127.0.0.1"))
```

## `sec-py/no-cleartext-http` — Requests go over HTTPS

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the server must serve HTTPS first, and the URL change has to follow it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-cleartext-http.md

### What it checks

`requests` and `httpx` are not called with an `http://` URL, except for localhost.

**Why:** The data, and any token in it, crosses the network readable and changeable by anyone on the path (CWE-319).

### How to fix

1. Change the URL to `https://`.
2. If the server cannot do HTTPS, put it behind a proxy that can, or reach it over a private tunnel.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import requests

resp = requests.get("http://api.example.com/data", timeout=5)
```

##### Do

```py
import requests

resp = requests.get("https://api.example.com/data", timeout=5)
```

## `sec-py/no-csrf-exempt` — No `@csrf_exempt`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (an endpoint that needs to be exempt (a webhook) needs its own authentication, which only the author can choose)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-csrf-exempt.md

### What it checks

A view is not decorated with `@csrf_exempt`.

**Why:** Without the token check any page the user visits can submit the form as the user (CWE-352).

### How to fix

1. Remove `@csrf_exempt` and send the token (`{% csrf_token %}`, or the `X-CSRFToken` header).
2. For a webhook, authenticate the sender (a signed header) and keep the exemption on that one view with a comment saying why.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from django.views.decorators.csrf import csrf_exempt

@csrf_exempt
def update(request):
    ...
```

##### Do

```py
def update(request):
    ...
```

## `sec-py/no-dynamic-import` — A request value does not choose a module or attribute

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the allow-list of names is the author's)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-dynamic-import.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not passed to `__import__`, `importlib.import_module` or `getattr`.

**Why:** The client then picks which module is loaded or which attribute is read or called, including ones that run commands (CWE-470). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Map the client's value to a fixed dict of allowed handlers: `HANDLERS = {"csv": export_csv}`; `HANDLERS[name]`.
2. Reject a name that is not a key.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def run(request):
    action = request.GET["action"]
    return getattr(handlers, action)()
```

##### Do

```py
def run(request):
    return HANDLERS[request.GET["action"]]()
```

## `sec-py/no-exec-eval` — `exec`, `eval` and `compile` of a non-literal

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the safe replacement (`ast.literal_eval`, a lookup table, a parser) depends on what the string is for)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-exec-eval.md

### What it checks

`exec`, `eval` and `compile` are not given a value that is not a string literal.

**Why:** The string is run as code, so whoever controls it controls the program (CWE-94).

### How to fix

1. For a literal (a number, a list, a dict), call `ast.literal_eval`.
2. For a choice among behaviours, map the input to a function through a dict.
3. For arithmetic or expressions, use a parser built for it, not the interpreter.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
result = eval(user_text)
```

##### Do

```py
import ast

result = ast.literal_eval(user_text)
```

## `sec-py/no-format-string-injection` — A request value is not a format string

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the template has to be a literal, which needs the format string moved out of the request)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-format-string-injection.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not the receiver of `.format`.

**Why:** A field such as `{obj.__class__.__init__.__globals__[SECRET]}` reads attributes of the arguments, so the client reads secrets (CWE-134). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Make the template a literal and pass the request value as an argument: `"Hello {}".format(name)`.
2. For client-written templates use `string.Template(...).safe_substitute(...)`, which has no attribute access.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def greet(request):
    return request.GET["tpl"].format(user)
```

##### Do

```py
def greet(request):
    return "Hello {}".format(request.GET["name"])
```

## `sec-py/no-hardcoded-crypto-key` — No keys or IVs in the source

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the key comes from (a key store, an environment variable) is a deployment decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-hardcoded-crypto-key.md

### What it checks

A cipher key, HMAC key, IV or nonce is not a literal.

**Why:** A key in the source is known to everyone who can read the source, and a fixed IV or nonce breaks the cipher's guarantees (CWE-321, CWE-329).

### How to fix

1. Generate keys with `os.urandom` or the library (`Fernet.generate_key()`) once, and store them in a secret manager or an environment variable.
2. Make a fresh random IV or nonce for every message (`os.urandom(12)`) and store it beside the ciphertext.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

f = Fernet(b"ZmFrZWtleWZha2VrZXlmYWtla2V5ZmFrZWtleTA9")
```

##### Do

```py
import os
from cryptography.fernet import Fernet

f = Fernet(os.environ["FERNET_KEY"])
```

## `sec-py/no-hardcoded-secret` — No secrets in the source

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the secret lives instead (environment, secret manager) is a decision, and the leaked one must be rotated)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-hardcoded-secret.md

### What it checks

A password, key or token is not a string literal in the code, and a cloud access key is not pasted into it.

**Why:** The source goes to every clone, build log and backup, so the secret does too, and revoking it means a release (CWE-798).

### How to fix

1. Rotate the secret: it is in version control now.
2. Read it at start-up: `os.environ["DB_PASSWORD"]`, or from your secret manager.
3. Keep local values in an untracked `.env` file.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
DB_PASSWORD = "hunter2-prod"
```

##### Do

```py
import os

DB_PASSWORD = os.environ["DB_PASSWORD"]
```

## `sec-py/no-header-injection` — A request value is not a response header

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to reject, strip or encode the value depends on what the header is for)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-header-injection.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not written into a response header or a cookie value without its line breaks removed.

**Why:** A CR or LF in the value ends the header and starts a new one, so an attacker can add headers or a second response (CWE-113). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Reject a value that contains `\r` or `\n`: `if "\n" in value or "\r" in value: abort(400)`.
2. Or percent-encode it: `urllib.parse.quote(value)`.
3. Modern servers and frameworks refuse newlines in headers; do not rely on that.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def view(request):
    resp = make_response("ok")
    resp.headers["X-Name"] = request.args["name"]
    return resp
```

##### Do

```py
def view(request):
    resp = make_response("ok")
    resp.headers["X-Name"] = quote(request.args["name"])
    return resp
```

## `sec-py/no-insecure-protocol` — No Telnet, FTP or SNMP v1/v2

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the replacement (SSH or SFTP, FTPS, SNMPv3) needs the server to support it)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-insecure-protocol.md

### What it checks

`telnetlib`, `ftplib` and SNMP community strings (v1/v2c) are not used.

**Why:** These send credentials and data in clear text, so anyone on the path reads and changes them (CWE-319).

### How to fix

1. Use SSH or SFTP (`paramiko`, `asyncssh`) instead of Telnet and FTP, or `ftplib.FTP_TLS` for FTPS.
2. Use SNMPv3 (`UsmUserData` with authentication and privacy) instead of a community string.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import ftplib

ftp = ftplib.FTP(host)
```

##### Do

```py
import paramiko

client = paramiko.SSHClient()
```

## `sec-py/no-insecure-random` — `secrets` for tokens, not `random`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`secrets` has different functions (`token_hex`, `choice`, `randbelow`), so the call has to be chosen, not renamed)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-insecure-random.md

### What it checks

A password, token, key, nonce or code is not made with the `random` module.

**Why:** `random` is a predictable generator, so a few outputs reveal the rest (CWE-338).

### How to fix

1. Use `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)` or `secrets.token_hex(16)` for a token.
2. Use `secrets.choice` for a character picked from an alphabet, `secrets.randbelow(n)` for a number.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import random

reset_token = random.getrandbits(64)
```

##### Do

```py
import secrets

reset_token = secrets.token_hex(16)
```

##### Fixed

```py
import random

reset_token = secrets.token_hex(16)
```

## `sec-py/no-insecure-tempfile` — `mkstemp` instead of `mktemp`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`mkstemp` returns an open file descriptor and a path, not just a name, so the surrounding code changes)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-insecure-tempfile.md

### What it checks

Temporary files are made with `tempfile.mkstemp`, `NamedTemporaryFile` or `TemporaryDirectory`, not `mktemp`, and not at a fixed path under `/tmp`.

**Why:** `mktemp` returns a name without creating the file, so another user can create it first and the program then writes into a file they control (CWE-377).

### How to fix

1. Use `with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False) as f:` and write through `f`.
2. Use `tempfile.mkdtemp()` or `TemporaryDirectory()` for a directory.
3. Never build a path under `/tmp` by hand.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import tempfile

path = tempfile.mktemp()
```

##### Do

```py
import tempfile

path = tempfile.mkstemp()[1]
```

##### Fixed

```py
import tempfile

path = tempfile.mkstemp()[1]
```

## `sec-py/no-ldap-injection` — LDAP filters are not built from strings

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the escaping function belongs to the LDAP library in use)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-ldap-injection.md

### What it checks

An LDAP search filter is not made with an f-string, `%`, `+` or `.format`.

**Why:** A value with `*`, `)` or `(` in it changes which entries the filter matches, which can turn a login check into a match-all (CWE-90).

### How to fix

1. Escape each value: `ldap3.utils.conv.escape_filter_chars(value)` or `ldap.filter.escape_filter_chars(value)`.
2. Or build the filter with `ldap.filter.filter_format("(uid=%s)", [value])`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
conn.search_s(base, ldap.SCOPE_SUBTREE, f"(uid={name})")
```

##### Do

```py
conn.search_s(base, ldap.SCOPE_SUBTREE, filter_format("(uid=%s)", [name]))
```

## `sec-py/no-llm-output-to-sink` — Model output is not run or rendered

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (what to do with the output instead (parse it against a schema, pick from a fixed list of actions) is a design choice)
- **Severity when named:** `warn` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-llm-output-to-sink.md

### What it checks

The reply of an OpenAI, Anthropic or LangChain call does not reach `exec`, `eval`, a subprocess, SQL or `mark_safe`.

**Why:** A model's output is shaped by its input, so a prompt written by an attacker becomes code, a command, a query or a script (CWE-94).

### How to fix

1. Ask the model for structured output and validate it against a schema.
2. Map the answer to a fixed list of actions the program already has; never pass it to a sink as text.
3. Escape it before it goes into HTML; use parameters for SQL.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
reply = client.chat.completions.create(model=m, messages=msgs)
exec(reply.choices[0].message.content)
```

##### Do

```py
reply = client.chat.completions.create(model=m, messages=msgs)
action = reply.choices[0].message.content.strip()
if action in ACTIONS:
    ACTIONS[action]()
```

## `sec-py/no-log-injection` — A request value is not logged raw

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to strip, escape or reject the value depends on how the log is read)
- **Severity when named:** `warn` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-log-injection.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not passed to a logger without its line breaks removed.

**Why:** A CR or LF in the value writes a line that looks like another log entry, so an attacker can forge audit records (CWE-117). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Pass the value through a helper that strips the line breaks, such as `clean(value)` with `text.replace("\r", "").replace("\n", " ")`; a method called on the request value itself is still seen as the request value.
2. Or log it as structured data (`extra={"name": value}`) and use a JSON formatter that escapes it.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def view(request):
    logger.info("login %s", request.POST["user"])
```

##### Do

```py
def clean(text):
    return text.replace("\r", "").replace("\n", " ")

def view(request):
    logger.info("login %s", clean(request.POST["user"]))
```

## `sec-py/no-mako` — No Mako templates

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (moving to another engine (or turning on `default_filters`) changes every template)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-mako.md

### What it checks

`mako.template.Template` is not used.

**Why:** Mako does not escape output unless told to, so every `${value}` is a script waiting for a hostile value (CWE-79).

### How to fix

1. Use Jinja2 with `autoescape=True`.
2. If you keep Mako, pass `default_filters=["h"]` to `Template` / `TemplateLookup`, and review each `|n`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from mako.template import Template

t = Template(source)
```

##### Do

```py
from jinja2 import Environment

env = Environment(autoescape=True)
```

## `sec-py/no-mark-safe` — No `mark_safe` of dynamic text

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the right fix is escaping the parts (`format_html`, `escape`) or rendering through a template, not removing the call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-mark-safe.md

### What it checks

`mark_safe`, `SafeString`, `Markup` and `format_html` are not given a value that is not a literal.

**Why:** They switch HTML escaping off for that value, so any part of it that came from a user is a script (CWE-79).

### How to fix

1. Build HTML with `format_html("<b>{}</b>", value)`: it escapes `value` and trusts only the literal.
2. Or render a template with autoescape on.
3. Use `mark_safe` only on a literal, or on text you produced by escaping.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from django.utils.safestring import mark_safe

html = mark_safe("<b>" + name + "</b>")
```

##### Do

```py
from django.utils.html import format_html

html = format_html("<b>{}</b>", name)
```

## `sec-py/no-mass-assignment` — A request is not splatted into a model

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (which fields a client may set is the author's decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-mass-assignment.md

### What it checks

`Model(**request.POST)`, `Model.objects.create(**request.data)` and `update(**request.json)` are not used, and a `ModelForm` or serializer does not set `fields = "__all__"`.

**Why:** The client chooses which columns are set, so it can set `is_staff`, `owner_id` or a price (CWE-915).

### How to fix

1. List the allowed fields: `fields = ["title", "body"]`.
2. Build the model from named values: `Post.objects.create(title=data["title"], owner=request.user)`.
3. Mark server-only fields `read_only_fields`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def create(request):
    return Post.objects.create(**request.POST)
```

##### Do

```py
def create(request):
    return Post.objects.create(title=request.POST["title"], owner=request.user)
```

## `sec-py/no-nosql-injection` — A request is not a MongoDB query

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (which fields the client may filter on, and their types, are the author's decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-nosql-injection.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not used whole as a `pymongo` filter, and a `$where` expression is not built from a request value.

**Why:** A JSON body such as `{"$ne": null}` or `{"$gt": ""}` in a query field matches every document, and `$where` runs JavaScript (CWE-943). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Build the filter yourself from named fields: `{"name": str(request.json["name"])}`; `str()` stops an operator object from getting through.
2. Validate the body against a schema (pydantic, marshmallow) before it reaches the query.
3. Do not use `$where`; express the condition with query operators.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def find(request):
    return db.users.find_one(request.json)
```

##### Do

```py
def find(request):
    name = str(request.json["name"])
    return db.users.find_one({"name": name})
```

## `sec-py/no-open-redirect` — A request value is not a redirect target

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the allowed destinations depend on the application)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-open-redirect.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not passed to `redirect`, `HttpResponseRedirect` or `RedirectResponse`.

**Why:** A link on another site can send your users to a look-alike page that starts from yours (CWE-601). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Redirect to a named route (`redirect(url_for("home"))`) and take only an id from the client.
2. Or check the target: Django `url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(url, allowed_hosts={request.get_host()})`; elsewhere require a path that starts with a single `/`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def login(request):
    nxt = request.args.get("next")
    return redirect(nxt)
```

##### Do

```py
def login(request):
    target = SAFE_TARGETS.get(request.args.get("next"), "/")
    return redirect(target)
```

## `sec-py/no-partial-path` — A program is started by its full path

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the absolute path differs by system, so it has to come from configuration or `shutil.which` at start-up)
- **Severity when named:** `warn` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `warn`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-partial-path.md

### What it checks

A subprocess is not started with a bare program name such as `"git"`.

**Why:** The shell looks the name up in `PATH`, so a program of the same name in an earlier folder runs instead (CWE-426).

### How to fix

1. Resolve it once at start-up: `GIT = shutil.which("git")`, and fail if it is `None`.
2. Or put the absolute path in configuration.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import subprocess

subprocess.run(["git", "status"])
```

##### Do

```py
import subprocess

subprocess.run(["/usr/bin/git", "status"])
```

## `sec-py/no-path-traversal` — A request value is not a file path

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the safe form (a lookup by id, a resolved path checked against a base folder) depends on the storage layout)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-path-traversal.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not passed to `open`, `send_file`, `send_from_directory` or `FileResponse` as a path.

**Why:** `../../etc/passwd` in the value reads any file the process can (CWE-22). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Look the file up by an id the program issued, not by a name the client chose.
2. Or resolve the path and check it stays inside the base folder: `p = (BASE / name).resolve(); p.relative_to(BASE.resolve())`.
3. Flask: use `send_from_directory(BASE, secure_filename(name))`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def download(request):
    name = request.GET["file"]
    return open(name, "rb")
```

##### Do

```py
def download(request):
    name = request.GET["file"]
    path = (BASE / name).resolve()
    path.relative_to(BASE.resolve())
    return open(path, "rb")
```

## `sec-py/no-prompt-injection` — A request value is not written into a system prompt

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (what goes in the system role and what goes in the user role is a design decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-prompt-injection.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not part of the system prompt of a language-model call.

**Why:** The model cannot tell your instructions from the user's text, so a user can rewrite the rules the system prompt sets (CWE-1427). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Keep the system prompt a constant.
2. Send the user's text as a separate `user` message, never concatenated into the system one.
3. Treat the model's answer as untrusted too (see `sec-py/no-llm-output-to-sink`).

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def ask(request):
    topic = request.GET["topic"]
    return client.messages.create(system=f"You help with {topic}.", messages=msgs)
```

##### Do

```py
def ask(request):
    msgs = [{"role": "user", "content": request.GET["topic"]}]
    return client.messages.create(system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, messages=msgs)
```

## `sec-py/no-pycrypto` — No `pycrypto`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the replacement package changes the import path and some call signatures)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-pycrypto.md

### What it checks

`Crypto` is not imported from the unmaintained `pycrypto` package.

**Why:** `pycrypto` has had no release since 2013 and carries known flaws, including a weak random generator and a buffer overflow (CWE-1104).

### How to fix

1. Prefer `cryptography` (`pip install cryptography`).
2. `pycryptodomex` is a maintained drop-in with the package name `Cryptodome`: change `Crypto` to `Cryptodome`.
3. `pycryptodome` (not `x`) also installs a package named `Crypto`; if that is what you use, switch to `Cryptodome` so this rule can tell them apart.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from Crypto.Cipher import AES
```

##### Do

```py
from Cryptodome.Cipher import AES
```

## `sec-py/no-reflected-xss` — A request value is not written into the response as it is

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (escaping the value or rendering a template are both fixes; which fits depends on the response)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-reflected-xss.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not passed to `HttpResponse`, `make_response` or `HTMLResponse`, or built into a returned string, without escaping.

**Why:** The page then contains whatever the client sent, including a script (CWE-79). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Escape it: `markupsafe.escape(value)` or Django's `django.utils.html.escape`.
2. Or render a template with autoescape on and pass the value in.
3. If the response is not HTML, set `Content-Type: text/plain` or `application/json`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def hello(request):
    return HttpResponse(request.GET["name"])
```

##### Do

```py
def hello(request):
    return HttpResponse(escape(request.GET["name"]))
```

## `sec-py/no-regex-injection` — A request value is not a regular expression

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`re.escape` turns the value into a literal search; a client that is meant to send a pattern needs a length limit and a timeout instead)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-regex-injection.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not used as the pattern of `re.compile`, `re.search`, `re.match` or the other `re` functions.

**Why:** The client can write a pattern that takes exponential time (a ReDoS) or changes what the search matches (CWE-730, CWE-1333). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. If the value is text to look for, wrap it in `re.escape(value)`.
2. If the client must send a pattern, limit its length and run it with a timeout (the `regex` package's `timeout=`).

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import re

def find(request, text):
    return re.search(request.GET["q"], text)
```

##### Do

```py
import re

def find(request, text):
    return re.search(re.escape(request.GET["q"]), text)
```

## `sec-py/no-secret-in-log` — Secrets are not logged

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (whether to drop the value or mask it depends on what the log is for)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-secret-in-log.md

### What it checks

A value named `password`, `token` or `secret` is not written to a log.

**Why:** Logs are kept longer and read by more people than the secret was meant for (CWE-532).

### How to fix

1. Remove the value from the message.
2. Log an id or `"set"/"missing"`, or a masked form such as the last four characters.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
logger.info("login with password %s", password)
```

##### Do

```py
logger.info("login for user %s", username)
```

## `sec-py/no-shell` — A shell command built from data

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (dropping `shell=True` only works when the command is already a list of arguments; a string command must be split)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-shell.md

### What it checks

A subprocess is not started with `shell=True`, and `os.system` / `os.popen` are not given a value that is not a literal.

**Why:** The command line goes through the shell, so a quote, `;` or `$(…)` in any part of it runs another command (CWE-78).

### How to fix

1. Pass the command as a list: `subprocess.run(["ls", "-l", path])`.
2. Remove `shell=True`.
3. Replace `os.system(cmd)` with `subprocess.run([...], check=True)`; use `shlex.split` only for a trusted fixed string.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import subprocess

subprocess.run(["ls", path], shell=True)
```

##### Do

```py
import subprocess

subprocess.run(["ls", path])
```

## `sec-py/no-silent-except` — Errors are not swallowed

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (what to do with the error (log, retry, stop) is a decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-silent-except.md

### What it checks

An `except` that catches everything (bare, `Exception` or `BaseException`) does not just `pass` or `continue`.

**Why:** A failure that is dropped hides a broken check or a failed login step, and the code goes on as though it had worked (CWE-703).

### How to fix

1. Catch the specific exceptions you expect.
2. Log the others with `logger.exception("…")` and let them go on or re-raise.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
try:
    check(token)
except Exception:
    pass
```

##### Do

```py
try:
    check(token)
except InvalidToken:
    logger.warning("bad token")
```

## `sec-py/no-sql-string` — SQL built from a string

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (which placeholder style the driver takes, and where each value goes, depends on the driver)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-sql-string.md

### What it checks

A SQL statement is not built with an f-string, `%`, `+` or `.format`; the values go in as parameters.

**Why:** A value that is part of the statement text can change the statement (CWE-89).

### How to fix

1. Write the statement with placeholders: `cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = %s", (item_id,))`.
2. Pass the values as the second argument; the driver quotes them.
3. A table or column name cannot be a parameter: choose it from a fixed allow-list.
4. In Django use the ORM, `.raw(sql, params)` or `RawSQL(sql, params)`; give `.extra` parameters through `params=`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def find(cursor, name):
    cursor.execute(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '{name}'")
```

##### Do

```py
def find(cursor, name):
    cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = %s", (name,))
```

## `sec-py/no-ssrf` — A request value is not a URL to fetch

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (which hosts are allowed is a policy only the author knows)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-ssrf.md

### What it checks

A value from the request is not the URL given to `requests`, `httpx` or `urllib`.

**Why:** The server fetches whatever address the client names, including internal services and cloud metadata (CWE-918). This rule uses `from_source:`, which is not taint analysis: it sees a request value only in the function that reads it, never through a call or a parameter.

### How to fix

1. Take an id or a key from the client and map it to a URL you wrote.
2. Or parse the URL and check the scheme is `https` and the host is on an allow-list, then connect to the address you resolved (not the name again).
3. Refuse private, loopback and link-local addresses.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def fetch(request):
    url = request.args["url"]
    return requests.get(url, timeout=5)
```

##### Do

```py
def fetch(request):
    host = urlparse(request.args["url"]).hostname
    if host not in ALLOWED_HOSTS:
        abort(400)
    return requests.get(ALLOWED_HOSTS[host], timeout=5)
```

## `sec-py/no-stack-trace-response` — A stack trace is not sent to the client

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (what the client sees instead (a generic message and an error id) is a product decision)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-stack-trace-response.md

### What it checks

A response does not contain `traceback.format_exc()` or the text of the exception.

**Why:** The text names files, queries, library versions and sometimes values, which tells an attacker where to push (CWE-209).

### How to fix

1. Log it: `logger.exception("upload failed")`.
2. Return a generic message and an id the client can quote: `{"error": "internal error", "id": error_id}`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
def view():
    try:
        run()
    except Exception as e:
        return jsonify(error=str(e))
```

##### Do

```py
def view():
    try:
        run()
    except Exception:
        logger.exception("run failed")
        return jsonify(error="internal error")
```

## `sec-py/no-tls-bypass` — TLS certificate checks stay on

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the server may use a private CA, which needs the CA bundle passed as `verify=` rather than the check removed)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-tls-bypass.md

### What it checks

Certificate verification is not switched off (`verify=False`, `_create_unverified_context`), and an SSL context is not pinned to an old protocol.

**Why:** Without the check anyone on the network path can pose as the server and read or change the traffic (CWE-295).

### How to fix

1. Delete `verify=False`; if the server uses a private CA, pass its bundle: `verify="/etc/ssl/corp-ca.pem"`.
2. Use `ssl.create_default_context()` instead of `_create_unverified_context()`.
3. Never set `check_hostname = False` or `verify_mode = ssl.CERT_NONE`; set `minimum_version = ssl.TLSVersion.TLSv1_2` instead of an old `PROTOCOL_*`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import requests

resp = requests.get(url, verify=False, timeout=5)
```

##### Do

```py
import requests

resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5)
```

## `sec-py/no-trust-remote-code` — No `trust_remote_code=True`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (using a model that needs custom code means reviewing and vendoring that code, which is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-trust-remote-code.md

### What it checks

`from_pretrained`, `load_dataset` and `pipeline` are not called with `trust_remote_code=True`.

**Why:** The repository's Python files are downloaded and run on your machine, so whoever can push to it runs code in your process (CWE-94).

### How to fix

1. Remove `trust_remote_code=True`; use a model whose architecture is built into the library.
2. If you need the code, read it, copy it into your repository at a pinned commit, and load that instead.
3. At least pin `revision=` to a commit you reviewed.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(name, trust_remote_code=True)
```

##### Do

```py
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(name, revision=REVISION)
```

## `sec-py/no-unsafe-deserialize` — Deserialising with `pickle` and its relatives

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the replacement format (JSON, a schema, a signed payload) is a design choice)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-unsafe-deserialize.md

### What it checks

Data is not loaded with `pickle`, `cPickle`, `dill`, `marshal`, `shelve` or `jsonpickle`.

**Why:** Loading runs code chosen by whoever wrote the bytes, so untrusted input is remote code execution (CWE-502).

### How to fix

1. Use JSON (`json.loads`) or another data-only format, and validate the result against a schema.
2. If the bytes must be a pickle, sign them (`hmac`) and verify the signature before loading, or load only files the program itself wrote.
3. For model weights use `safetensors`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import pickle

obj = pickle.loads(payload)
```

##### Do

```py
import json

obj = json.loads(payload)
```

## `sec-py/no-weak-cipher` — No DES, RC4, Blowfish or ECB

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the new cipher changes key size, nonce handling and the stored format)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-weak-cipher.md

### What it checks

A weak cipher (DES, 3DES, ARC2, ARC4, Blowfish, CAST5, IDEA) or ECB mode is not used.

**Why:** The ciphers have small blocks or known attacks, and ECB encrypts equal blocks to equal output, so the data's structure shows through (CWE-327).

### How to fix

1. Use `cryptography`'s `AESGCM` or `ChaCha20Poly1305`: they encrypt and authenticate.
2. A new random nonce for every message; never reuse one with the same key.
3. Re-encrypt stored data under the new scheme.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from Crypto.Cipher import AES

cipher = AES.new(key, AES.MODE_ECB)
```

##### Do

```py
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.ciphers.aead import AESGCM

cipher = AESGCM(key)
```

## `sec-py/no-weak-hash` — No MD5 or SHA-1 for security

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (whether the digest is used for security (use SHA-256) or only as a checksum (say so) is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-weak-hash.md

### What it checks

`hashlib.md5` and `hashlib.sha1` pass `usedforsecurity=False`, or are replaced by SHA-256.

**Why:** Both can be forged by collision, so they prove nothing about who wrote the data (CWE-327).

### How to fix

1. If the digest guards integrity or identity, use `hashlib.sha256` or `hashlib.blake2b`.
2. If it is only a cache key or checksum, pass `usedforsecurity=False` and say so in a comment.
3. For passwords see `sec-py/password-hash-effort`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import hashlib

digest = hashlib.md5(data).hexdigest()
```

##### Do

```py
import hashlib

digest = hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
```

## `sec-py/no-wildcard-injection` — A shell wildcard after `tar`, `chown`, `chmod` or `rsync`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the files have to be listed (`glob`) and passed after `--`, which changes the call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-wildcard-injection.md

### What it checks

A command that runs `tar`, `chown`, `chmod` or `rsync` on `*` is not started through a shell.

**Why:** A file named `--checkpoint-action=exec=sh x.sh` in the folder is expanded by the shell into an option, so whoever can create files there runs commands (CWE-155).

### How to fix

1. List the files in Python: `files = sorted(glob.glob("*.txt"))`.
2. Pass them as a list after `--`: `subprocess.run(["tar", "cf", out, "--", *files])`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import os

os.system("tar cf backup.tar *")
```

##### Do

```py
import subprocess

subprocess.run(["tar", "cf", "backup.tar", "--", *files], check=True)
```

## `sec-py/no-world-writable` — No world-writable files

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the right mode depends on who has to write the file)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-world-writable.md

### What it checks

`os.chmod` and `os.umask` do not give write access to everyone.

**Why:** Any local user can then change the file, which for a script, config or socket means running code as its owner (CWE-732).

### How to fix

1. Use `0o600` for a private file, `0o644` for one others read, `0o755` for a program.
2. Never set the others' write bit.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import os

os.chmod(path, 0o777)
```

##### Do

```py
import os

os.chmod(path, 0o600)
```

##### Fixed

```py
import os

os.chmod(path, 0o600)
```

## `sec-py/no-xml-unsafe-parser` — XML is parsed with `defusedxml`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`defusedxml` has to be installed and imported, and it refuses documents the standard parser accepts)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-xml-unsafe-parser.md

### What it checks

XML from outside the program is parsed with `defusedxml`, not with `xml.etree`, `minidom`, `sax` or `lxml`.

**Why:** The standard parsers expand entities, so a crafted document can read local files, reach the network or exhaust memory (CWE-611).

### How to fix

1. Install `defusedxml` and import it: `import defusedxml.ElementTree as ET`.
2. Call the same function on it: `ET.fromstring(text)`.
3. For `minidom`, `sax` or `pulldom`, import the module of the same name from `defusedxml`; for `lxml`, build the parser with `resolve_entities=False, no_network=True`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

tree = ET.parse(path)
```

##### Do

```py
import defusedxml.ElementTree as ET

tree = ET.parse(path)
```

##### Fixed

```py
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

tree = defusedxml.ElementTree.parse(path)
```

## `sec-py/no-xmlrpc` — No `xmlrpc` without `defusedxml`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the patch has to run once before any xmlrpc object exists, and where that is depends on the program's start-up)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-xmlrpc.md

### What it checks

An `xmlrpc` client or server is not created without `defusedxml.xmlrpc.monkey_patch()` in the program.

**Why:** `xmlrpc` parses XML with the standard parser, so a crafted request or response carries an entity expansion bomb or reads files (CWE-776).

### How to fix

1. Add `import defusedxml.xmlrpc` and call `defusedxml.xmlrpc.monkey_patch()` once, before any `xmlrpc` object is made.
2. Or move the API to JSON over HTTP.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from xmlrpc.client import ServerProxy

proxy = ServerProxy(url)
```

##### Do

```py
import requests

resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=10)
```

## `sec-py/no-xpath-injection` — XPath expressions are not built from strings

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the expression has to be rewritten around `$name` variables, and which parts are values is the author's call)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/no-xpath-injection.md

### What it checks

An XPath expression is not made with an f-string, `%`, `+` or `.format`; values go in as XPath variables.

**Why:** A quote in the value ends the string in the expression and the rest of the value is read as XPath (CWE-643).

### How to fix

1. Write the expression with variables: `tree.xpath("//user[@name=$name]", name=name)` (lxml).
2. ElementTree has no variables: select by a simple path and compare the attribute in Python.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
nodes = tree.xpath(f"//user[@name='{name}']")
```

##### Do

```py
nodes = tree.xpath("//user[@name=$name]", name=name)
```

## `sec-py/paramiko-host-key` — SSH host keys are checked

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (where the known host keys come from is deployment-specific)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/paramiko-host-key.md

### What it checks

`paramiko` is not told to accept unknown host keys with `AutoAddPolicy` or `WarningPolicy`.

**Why:** A connection to an impostor goes through unnoticed, and the credentials are handed to it (CWE-295).

### How to fix

1. Call `client.load_system_host_keys()` or `load_host_keys(path)`.
2. Use `client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.RejectPolicy())`.
3. Put the server's key in `known_hosts` ahead of time.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.AutoAddPolicy())
```

##### Do

```py
client.load_system_host_keys()
client.set_missing_host_key_policy(paramiko.RejectPolicy())
```

## `sec-py/password-hash-effort` — Passwords are hashed with a slow function

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (moving to Argon2 or bcrypt means rehashing at the next login and changing the stored format)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/password-hash-effort.md

### What it checks

A password is not hashed with a plain `hashlib` digest, `pbkdf2_hmac` runs at least 600 000 iterations, and `bcrypt` uses at least 10 rounds.

**Why:** A fast hash lets an attacker who has the table test billions of guesses per second (CWE-916).

### How to fix

1. Use `argon2-cffi` (`PasswordHasher().hash(password)`) or `bcrypt.hashpw(password, bcrypt.gensalt(rounds=12))`.
2. If you must use PBKDF2, use SHA-256 with at least 600 000 iterations (OWASP).
3. Rehash old entries when a user logs in.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import hashlib

stored = hashlib.sha256(password.encode()).hexdigest()
```

##### Do

```py
from argon2 import PasswordHasher

stored = PasswordHasher().hash(password)
```

## `sec-py/requests-timeout` — HTTP requests have a timeout

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (the right timeout depends on the service; the suggested value is a starting point)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/requests-timeout.md

### What it checks

`requests` and `httpx` calls pass `timeout=`.

**Why:** `requests` waits forever by default, so one stuck server holds a worker for good and a flood of slow responses exhausts them (CWE-400).

### How to fix

1. Pass `timeout=` in seconds, or a `(connect, read)` tuple.
2. Keep the value in one setting if several calls share it.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import requests

resp = requests.get(url)
```

##### Do

```py
import requests

resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
```

##### Fixed

```py
import requests

resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
```

## `sec-py/tarfile-filter` — Archive extraction uses `filter="data"`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`filter="data"` refuses members that carry device files or special permissions some archives need)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/tarfile-filter.md

### What it checks

`TarFile.extractall` and `shutil.unpack_archive` pass `filter="data"`.

**Why:** A member named `../../etc/cron.d/x`, an absolute path or a symlink writes outside the target folder (CWE-22).

### How to fix

1. Pass `filter="data"` (Python 3.12, and the 3.8–3.11 security releases).
2. Pass it to `shutil.unpack_archive(…, filter="data")` too.
3. Extract into a fresh folder, and never run as root.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import tarfile

with tarfile.open(path) as tar:
    tar.extractall(dest)
```

##### Do

```py
import tarfile

with tarfile.open(path) as tar:
    tar.extractall(dest, filter="data")
```

##### Fixed

```py
import tarfile

with tarfile.open(path) as tar:
    tar.extractall(dest, filter="data")
```

## `sec-py/torch-load-weights-only` — `torch.load` with `weights_only=True`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`weights_only=True` refuses checkpoints that hold arbitrary objects; those need a conversion to `safetensors`)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/torch-load-weights-only.md

### What it checks

`torch.load` is called with `weights_only=True`.

**Why:** Without it the file is unpickled, so a model file from anywhere else runs code on load (CWE-502).

### How to fix

1. Add `weights_only=True`.
2. If the checkpoint holds more than tensors, convert it once with a trusted environment and keep it as `safetensors`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
import torch

model = torch.load(path)
```

##### Do

```py
import torch

model = torch.load(path, weights_only=True)
```

##### Fixed

```py
import torch

model = torch.load(path, weights_only=True)
```

## `sec-py/upload-secure-filename` — Uploaded files are saved under a safe name

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (`secure_filename` removes characters a name may legitimately have, and returns an empty string for some names, which needs handling)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/upload-secure-filename.md

### What it checks

A file from a request is not saved under the name the client gave it.

**Why:** The name can be `../../app.py` or an absolute path, so the upload overwrites a file outside the upload folder (CWE-434, CWE-22).

### How to fix

1. Import `from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename`.
2. Use `secure_filename(file.filename)`, and refuse an empty result.
3. Better: store the file under a name you generate (a UUID) and keep the client's name as data.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

file.save(os.path.join(UPLOADS, file.filename))
```

##### Do

```py
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

file.save(os.path.join(UPLOADS, secure_filename(file.filename)))
```

##### Fixed

```py
from werkzeug.utils import secure_filename

file.save(os.path.join(UPLOADS, secure_filename(file.filename)))
```

## `sec-py/urlopen-scheme` — `urlopen` of a value that may be `file://`

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `manual` (the allowed schemes and hosts are policy)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/urlopen-scheme.md

### What it checks

`urllib.request.urlopen` and `urlretrieve` are not given a value that is not an `http(s)` literal.

**Why:** `urlopen` also opens `file://` and `ftp://` URLs, so a value that is not checked can read local files (CWE-22, CWE-918).

### How to fix

1. Parse the URL and check `scheme in ("http", "https")` before opening it.
2. Or use `requests`, which supports only HTTP(S), with a `timeout`.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from urllib.request import urlopen

data = urlopen(url).read()
```

##### Do

```py
from urllib.request import urlopen

data = urlopen("https://example.com/data").read()
```

## `sec-py/weak-key-size` — RSA and DSA keys are at least 2048 bits

- **Pack:** `codelaw-rules-security-python` · **Languages:** Python
- **Fix:** `suggest` (a longer key makes existing signatures and certificates incompatible and slows each operation)
- **Severity when named:** `error` · **Turned on by:** `codelaw:sec-py/recommended` at `error` · `codelaw:sec-py/strict` at `error`
- **Page:** https://github.com/arpitarya/codelaw/blob/main/docs/rules/sec-py/weak-key-size.md

### What it checks

An RSA or DSA key is not generated shorter than 2048 bits, and an elliptic curve is at least 224 bits.

**Why:** Short keys can be factored or searched with hardware that is within reach (CWE-326).

### How to fix

1. Use at least 2048 bits for RSA and DSA, 3072 for keys that must last past 2030.
2. Use `ec.SECP256R1()` or Ed25519 for new keys.
3. Re-issue certificates signed with the old key.

### Examples

#### Python

##### Don't

```py
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa

key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=1024)
```

##### Do

```py
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import rsa

key = rsa.generate_private_key(public_exponent=65537, key_size=2048)
```

##### Fixed

